author: The Hill

title: Utah charges Kalshi, executives over illegal online gambling
content: Utah has filed criminal charges against prediction market platform Kalshi, CEO Tarek Mansour, and Chief Operating Officer Luana Lopes Lara. The state alleges the individuals illegally profited from promoting and offering online gambling within the jurisdiction. The defendants face 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count as part of this legal action.
summary: Utah has brought criminal charges against Kalshi and its CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara for allegedly profiting from illegal online gambling in the state. The charges include 13 felony counts and one misdemeanor count.
author: The Hill

title: National Links Trust to End Operations at East Potomac Golf Links on Nov. 15
content: The National Links Trust announced it will cease operations at East Potomac Golf Links, Washington’s most popular public golf course, on Nov. 15. In a Thursday statement, the NLT noted that a new long‑term lease with the Interior Department and the National Park Service to manage and operate the site is part of the transition, as President Trump is reportedly eyeing the property for redevelopment.
summary: The National Links Trust announced it will cease operating the East Potomac Golf Links, Washington’s most popular public golf course, on Nov. 15. The move comes as President Trump eyes the property for redevelopment and the NLT referenced a new long‑term lease with the Interior Department and National Park Service.
author: The Hill

title: Missouri abortion ban and California billionaire tax proposals appear on state ballots
content: Missouri and California voters will decide on significant ballot measures, including potential bans on abortion, new taxes on billionaire wealth, and restrictions concerning transgender individuals. In Missouri, the proposed abortion ban would follow the removal of a previous ban two years prior. Meanwhile, California residents may vote to impose a 5% wealth tax on billionaires.
summary: Missouri voters could approve a ban on abortion, reversing a ban that was removed two years ago. California voters could approve a measure to tax billionaires at 5% of their wealth.
author: NPR Politics

title: Study: Nearly half of severely distressed AI users seek emotional support from chatbots
content: A new study reveals that nearly one-third of Israeli adults using generative AI tools seek emotional support, coping advice, or mental health assistance from platforms like ChatGPT and Gemini. Among those experiencing severe psychological distress, this figure rises to almost half. The research was conducted by Tel-Hai University of Kiryat Shmona in the Galilee along with collaborating institutions.
summary: A study found that almost one in three Israeli adults using generative AI tools seek emotional support or mental health assistance from platforms like ChatGPT. Among users experiencing severe psychological distress, the percentage seeking this support rose to nearly one in two.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Complex medication regimens linked to greater physician burden in home care
content: Patients receiving home-based medical care, often older adults with multiple chronic conditions, frequently experience polypharmacy, defined as the concurrent use of multiple medications. While this practice is prevalent in this population, the associated challenges of medication management extend beyond merely the number of prescribed drugs.
summary: Patients receiving home-based medical care are often older adults with multiple chronic conditions and prevalent polypharmacy. The challenges of medication management for these patients extend beyond the number of prescribed medications.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Flinders University warns autistic adults face elevated cybercrime risks
content: Flinders University experts warn that autistic adults face elevated risks of involvement in cyber-related crime. The research suggests these individuals may fall into such criminal activities unwittingly.
summary: Flinders University experts warn that autistic adults may have elevated risks of being involved in cyber-related crime. These individuals might fall into such crimes unwittingly.
author: Medical Xpress

title: GLP-1 drugs help bariatric surgery patients lose regained weight
content: A study involving researchers from the Regenstrief Institute, Indiana University, Purdue University, and the University of Florida suggests that GLP-1 medications may assist patients in losing weight regained after bariatric surgery. The research indicates that individuals prescribed these glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists lost more of their regained weight over six and 12 months compared to similar patients who did not use the drugs.
summary: A study by researchers at Regenstrief Institute, Indiana University, Purdue University, and the University of Florida found that GLP-1 medications benefit those who regain weight after bariatric surgery. Patients prescribed these drugs lost more regained weight over six and 12 months than comparable patients who did not use them.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Permanent DST bill passed by House could add two billion dark school commutes
content: The U.S. House of Representatives passed a bill last summer to make daylight saving time permanent in the United States, eliminating the practice of turning back the clocks each fall. Nineteen states, including Washington, have already preapproved this change. If the bill is ultimately signed into law, the permanent daylight saving time would go into effect in those states.
summary: Permanent DST bill passed by House could add two billion dark school commutes.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Hidden brain rhythm in macaques challenges consciousness theories
content: New research by Janis Hesse at the University of California, Berkeley, and colleagues aims to address the mystery of how brains give rise to consciousness. The study, which involves macaque monkeys, suggests that a hidden brain rhythm challenges existing ideas about the origins of consciousness.
summary: New research by Janis Hesse at the University of California, Berkeley, and colleagues may help explain how brains give rise to consciousness. The study's insights are derived from research conducted on macaque monkeys.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Brain scans reveal silent strokes and benign tumors in healthy adults
content: In 2007, Dutch researchers scanned the brains of 2,000 individuals aged 45 and older who were living ordinary lives. The study revealed that seven percent of participants had signs of a stroke they were unaware of. Additionally, nearly two percent had a small bulge in a blood vessel, while a similar number possessed a benign tumor.
summary: A 2007 study in the Netherlands found that seven in every 100 adults aged 45 and over had signs of a stroke they were unaware of. The scan also identified small blood vessel bulges and benign tumors in nearly two in every 100 participants.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Iron-based MRI agent slows heart scarring in lab-grown human tissue
content:
A research group at Ikerbasque, led by Aitziber L. Cortajarena, has developed an iron-based magnetic resonance imaging contrast agent designed for both diagnostic and therapeutic applications. The team, specializing in Biomolecular Nanotechnology, tested this new agent on lab-grown human heart tissue to evaluate its efficacy in addressing cardiac fibrosis.

The study demonstrated that the agent accumulates specifically within fibrotic tissue. Additionally, the MRI signal intensity of the agent increased as the severity of the disease progressed. The research further confirmed that the contrast agent successfully slowed the progression of the condition in the tested tissue.
summary: The Biomolecular Nanotechnology research group, led by Ikerbasque research professor Aitziber L. Cortajarena, developed an iron‑based MRI contrast agent that accumulates in fibrotic heart tissue. In lab‑grown human heart tissue, the agent’s signal intensity rises with disease severity and it slows disease progression.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Concern over cut to Card Before You Leave mental health crisis scheme
content: Concern has been raised over a proposed cut to the Card Before You Leave scheme, which supports young people in mental health crises. The scheme guarantees that those presenting at a hospital emergency department receive a written appointment with specialists before they leave.
summary: There is concern about a cut to the Card Before You Leave scheme for young people's mental health crises. The scheme ensures that young people who present at a hospital emergency department in a mental health crisis receive a written appointment with specialists before leaving.
author: BBC Health

title: Europe’s central bank chief Christine Lagarde to step down nine months early
content: Christine Lagarde, the president of the European Central Bank, will step down from her role on 7 February 2027, nine months before her term was originally scheduled to end in October. The ECB announced the decision on Thursday, bringing an end to months of speculation regarding her future. Lagarde is currently viewed as a candidate to take over the World Economic Forum. This departure occurs while the eurozone continues to face challenges with weak growth and inflation.
summary: Europe’s central bank chief Christine Lagarde to step down nine months early.
author: Guardian Business

title: DoorDash to acquire Instacart for $17 billion
content: Acquisition will supercharge DoorDash’s grocery delivery, ‘one of the hardest things to get right online’, CEO says DoorDash is gobbling up Instacart in a $17bn acquisition that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. DoorDash said the Instacart brand name and app will remain, and Instacart shoppers can continue fulfilling orders for Instacart. Grocers can also choose to work with Instacart or DoorDash. Instacart customers will now have access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash, the company said.
summary: DoorDash is acquiring Instacart in a $17 billion deal that will supercharge its grocery delivery business. The Instacart brand and app will remain, and customers will gain access to 50,000 additional stores covered by DoorDash.
author: Guardian Business

title: FTC Orders Delta, Uber, and Nine Other Companies to Disclose Algorithmic Pricing Data
content:
The Federal Trade Commission has issued a demand to nine major US companies, including Delta, United, JetBlue, Lyft, Uber, DoorDash, Instacart, Target, and Walmart, to disclose how they utilize algorithms and loyalty programs. The regulator is seeking explanations for why these entities charge different prices for identical products or services and vary wages for drivers based on personal histories.

This inquiry follows prior investigations and lawsuits alleging that consumers face price discrimination based on their buying histories and that drivers receive different fares due to their personal records. The FTC’s move targets some of the nation’s largest airlines, ride-share platforms, and retailers to uncover the mechanisms behind these algorithmic pricing practices.
summary: The Federal Trade Commission is demanding that nine major companies, including Delta, Uber, and Walmart, explain how they use algorithms and loyalty programs to set variable prices and wages. This inquiry follows investigations and lawsuits alleging that consumers and drivers face different costs based on their personal histories.
author: Guardian Business

title: US GDP grows 3.4% in Q3, September inflation rises to 3.7%
content:
The US economy expanded at a 3.4% annualized rate in the third quarter, surpassing the 3.2% pace forecast by economists polled by Reuters. This data, released by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis on Thursday, coincided with reports that inflation accelerated to 3.7% in September. The release occurred less than a week before the midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress.

These economic figures contrast with a sharp deterioration in consumer sentiment as the elections approach. The Commerce Department data highlights a divergence between robust GDP growth and rising inflation, providing a mixed economic backdrop ahead of the upcoming vote.
summary: US GDP grows 3.4% in Q3, September inflation rises to 3.7%.
author: Guardian Business

title: Ralph Nader warns conditions are worse as he challenges Democrats ahead of 2026 midterms
content:
Ralph Nader, the former presidential candidate and consumer-rights advocate, argues that the issues driving his 2000 campaign are now more severe than ever ahead of the 2026 US midterm elections. He cites a corporate plutocracy, a broken healthcare system, massive inequality, and cash-soaked elections as key problems. Nader also notes that many people are angry about their inability to pay bills and are disgusted with lawmakers in Washington DC.

Nader states that these conditions are nearly identical to those that prompted his previous presidential run, which he describes as making him a political pariah in Washington. However, he asserts that the situation is now much, much worse. The former candidate emphasizes the need to “really change things for the working class” as he issues a challenge to Democrats in the upcoming election cycle.
summary: Ralph Nader states that issues like corporate power and broken healthcare are worse now than during his 2000 presidential run. He asserts these conditions will push him to challenge Democrats in the upcoming 2026 midterm elections.
author: Guardian Business

title: New harmonic increment method improves smooth approximations of minimum function
content:
A recent paper published in the Journal of Inequalities and Applications introduces a new method for improving smooth approximations of the minimum function. Prof. Thomas A. Weber demonstrates how a harmonic-increment transformation enhances these calculations for systems limited by their smallest input.

The technique brings any smooth estimate that lies strictly below the minimum closer to the actual value. Crucially, the improved estimate remains below the minimum, ensuring it stays a conservative estimate of a worst realization, or weakest link.
summary: A harmonic increment provides a new way to improve smooth approximations of the minimum function. In a recent paper, published in the Journal of Inequalities and Applications, Prof.
author: Phys.org

title: Emory physicists propose light method to detect anyons for quantum computing
content: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have developed a method to use light to detect the "spectral fingerprints" of anyons, which are exotic quasiparticles arising from the collective behavior of many electrons. Published in Physical Review Letters, this work provides a new tool for studying anyons, which have potential as fundamental building blocks for quantum computing.
summary: Theoretical physicists at Emory University have developed a method to use light to detect the spectral fingerprints of anyons. Their findings, published in Physical Review Letters, offer a new tool for studying these quasiparticles which hold potential as building blocks for quantum computing.
author: Phys.org

title: What makes forest protection work?
content: A new study by the Institute for Food and Resource Economics at the University of Bonn indicates that the success of nature conservation measures is partly determined by the credible enforcement of environmental laws.
summary: A new study from the Institute for Food and Resource Economics at the University of Bonn shows that the success of nature conservation measures depends partly on the credible enforcement of environmental laws.
author: Phys.org

title: Permanent DST bill puts U.S. schoolchildren at risk by forcing pre-sunrise commutes
content:
A new analysis published in Current Biology on October 29 warns that making daylight saving time permanent would endanger millions of U.S. schoolchildren. The study examines the implications of the Sunshine Protection Act, which the U.S. House passed in July 2026. According to the report, this legislation would force students to leave for school before sunrise for much of the academic year.

The analysis indicates that these earlier departure times coincide with periods when fatal crashes involving pedestrians are more likely. Consequently, the permanent shift to daylight saving time could significantly increase safety risks for children commuting to school in the dark.
summary: Permanent DST bill puts U.S. schoolchildren at risk by forcing pre-sunrise commutes.
author: Phys.org

title: Experts warn underpreparing for severe climate risks can cost the UK far more than overpreparing
content: Experts in climate, nature, health, national security and financial risk have co‑authored a commentary in Nature Climate Change urging a more integrated approach to UK government climate and nature risk assessments. They argue that conflicting advice can present policymakers with very different pictures of future risk severity, complicating decisions about the seriousness of action and the level of spending required. The authors warn that, for the United Kingdom, underpreparing for severe climate risks could cost far more than the expense of overpreparing.
summary: Experts warn underpreparing for severe climate risks can cost the UK far more than overpreparing.
author: Phys.org

title: Ultrathin carbon ribbons conduct electricity like metals in first successful synthesis
content: As modern electronic devices shrink, the metal electrical wires inside them face significant challenges. These conventional wires generate excessive heat and experience a massive spike in electrical resistance, which negatively affects overall performance as their size decreases.
summary: Scientists have achieved the first successful synthesis of ultrathin carbon ribbons that conduct electricity like metals. Conventional metal wires in shrinking electronic devices generate excessive heat and experience a spike in electrical resistance.
author: Phys.org

title: ISTA study links stars' evolutionary history to magnetic field estimates
content: A new study published in Astronomy & Astrophysics by researchers at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria (ISTA) highlights the impact of stellar evolutionary history on magnetic field estimates. Magnetic fields are present in many stars, including the sun, but remain poorly understood and are rarely included in stellar evolution models, which limits their accuracy. The research suggests that a star's "criminal" evolutionary history is crucial for correctly interpreting its internal magnetic fields.
summary: A new study by researchers at the Institute of Science and Technology Austria shows that a star's evolutionary history is crucial for interpreting its internal magnetic fields. The research, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, addresses why magnetic fields are too poorly understood to be reliably included in stellar evolution models.
author: Phys.org

title: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated
content: Quantum mechanics is distinguished by its probabilistic nature, a characteristic that sets it apart from other physical theories. A new analysis indicates that this specific property may originate from the mathematical foundations of the theory, running deeper than previously anticipated.
summary: Key oddity of quantum physics may run even deeper than anticipated.
author: New Scientist

title: Weakened brain signal may link schizophrenia symptoms
content: Scientists have identified a weakened brain signal that may link several seemingly unrelated schizophrenia symptoms, including sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and greater symptom severity. This discovery could help explain the disorder's underlying mechanisms and potentially facilitate earlier detection and the development of new treatments.
summary: Scientists identified a weakened brain signal that may connect sensory processing difficulties, disorganized speech, and symptom severity in schizophrenia. This discovery could help explain the disorder's mechanisms and lead to earlier detection and new treatments.
author: Science Daily

title: UIC study finds cranberry juice slows dental plaque bacteria regrowth
content:
Researchers at the University of Illinois Chicago have found that pure, unsweetened cranberry juice can help protect teeth from decay. The study revealed that the juice slows the regrowth of dental plaque bacteria and reduces their production of acids that damage tooth enamel. This discovery adds a new potential benefit to cranberry juice, which is already known for helping prevent urinary tract infections.

The protective effect may be attributed to naturally occurring compounds called proanthocyanidins. These substances interfere with harmful bacteria, thereby mitigating the acid production responsible for enamel erosion.
summary: Researchers at the University of Illinois Chicago found that pure, unsweetened cranberry juice reduces acid production and slows the regrowth of dental plaque bacteria. The effect is attributed to naturally occurring compounds called proanthocyanidins that interfere with harmful bacteria.
author: Science Daily

title: Less than 42 minutes of bright daylight linked to higher dementia risk
content: A study involving more than 87,000 adults indicates that higher daytime light exposure is associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia. The research found that longer exposure to bright light was linked to even greater reductions in this risk. Notably, getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily emerged as a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.
summary: A study of more than 87,000 adults found that higher daytime light exposure was associated with a 16% lower risk of dementia. Getting less than 42 minutes of bright daylight daily was a stronger predictor of dementia than six established risk factors.
author: Science Daily

title: 700,000-year-old elephant tooth found in Israel reveals lush prehistoric world
content: A 700,000-year-old straight-tusked elephant tooth discovered in northern Israel reveals a lush prehistoric environment where giant elephants and early humans coexisted. Found alongside ancient stone tools, the remarkably preserved artifact belonged to one of the largest land mammals of the Ice Age.
summary: A remarkably preserved straight-tusked elephant tooth dating back nearly 700,000 years was discovered in northern Israel alongside ancient stone tools. The find reveals a surprisingly lush prehistoric environment where giant elephants and early humans lived together.
author: Science Daily

title: 128,000-year-old ice found in Tibet could rewrite climate history
content: Ancient ice discovered high in Tibet is estimated to be more than 128,000 years old, preserving a climate record scientists previously believed was lost. This finding offers a rare glimpse into the last ice age and may reshape understanding of how glaciers survive dramatic global climate changes.
summary: Ancient ice discovered in Tibet is over 128,000 years old and preserves a record of Earth's climate previously thought lost. The finding offers insight into the last ice age and how glaciers survive dramatic global climate changes.
author: Science Daily

title: NASA Juno Finds Jupiter's Complex Plasma Shield Differs from Earth's
content: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has identified a complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions that Jupiter uses to defend against the solar wind. These findings highlight significant differences between Jupiter and Earth, potentially aiding scientists in understanding the massive shock waves generated by exploding stars.
summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft discovered that Jupiter uses a complex system of plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. These findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and may help scientists understand shock waves from exploding stars.
author: Science Daily

title: Mathematicians Find Flaw in Standard Model That Could Eliminate Need for Dark Energy
content:
Mathematicians have identified a potential fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, which could challenge the necessity of dark energy. Their calculations indicate that the mathematical framework describing cosmic expansion is inherently unstable. Consequently, the universe might accelerate naturally under Einstein’s original theory of gravity, rather than requiring an additional force to explain its expansion.

These findings also introduce questions regarding the assumption that our location in the universe is ordinary. By suggesting that cosmic acceleration can be explained without dark energy, the research proposes an alternative interpretation of the universe's dynamics based on existing gravitational theories.
summary: Mathematicians argue that the standard model of the universe contains a fundamental flaw that challenges the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity, raising questions about the ordinariness of our location in the universe.
author: Science Daily

title: Study Links Six Popular Sugar Substitutes to Faster Brain Aging
content: A study of nearly 13,000 adults found that individuals consuming the most artificial sweeteners experienced a 62% faster decline in memory and thinking skills. This decline was equivalent to approximately 1.6 additional years of brain aging. The research linked six popular sugar substitutes to this accelerated cognitive decline, raising concerns about long-term brain health effects, though causation was not established.
summary: Study Links Six Popular Sugar Substitutes to Faster Brain Aging.
author: Science Daily

title: Dame Sue Black Discusses Court Challenges in Forensic Anthropology Podcast
content:
Dame Sue Black, a leading forensic anthropologist, has served as an expert witness in numerous high-profile criminal cases. Her professional experience extends beyond the laboratory to active war zones and the aftermath of natural disasters, where she has identified victims’ bodies. In a podcast interview with Ian Sample, the professor discusses the challenges of testifying in court.

Black describes standing before a judge and jury as one of the most terrifying aspects of her career. She also addresses the reputational risks associated with presenting evidence in legal proceedings. Additionally, she offers insights into the potential future of forensic science. The podcast is available for order from the Guardian bookshop.
summary: Dame Sue Black, a leading forensic anthropologist, explains the fear and reputational risk of standing before a judge and jury in her Guardian podcast. She also discusses her work identifying victims in war zones, natural disasters, and the future of forensic science.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Welcomes Jared Spiers as Civil Servant After Contractor Transition
content:
Jared Spiers has transitioned from a contractor to a NASA civil servant at the agency’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi. This change occurred in June 2026 as part of an administrator’s directive aimed at strengthening technical core competencies within the civil service workforce. Spiers currently serves as an electrical engineering technician, a role he has held since graduating from Pearl River Community College in 2017, where he earned three associate degrees in instrumentation, electronics, and electrical technology. He began his career at NASA Stennis the Monday following his graduation.

Spiers has contributed to NASA’s lunar return mission through his work at the Thad Cochran Test Stand, a facility originally built to test Saturn V rocket stages during the Apollo Program. He helped prepare the stand for the Green Run test series of the first core stage for the Space Launch System rocket prior to the successful Artemis I test flight. His work also laid the foundation for the Artemis II test flight around the Moon in April 2026, during which the first astronauts to fly aboard the Orion spacecraft traveled farther in space than humans had before.

Currently, Spiers works 12-hour shifts starting at 6 a.m. as part of the team preparing the test stand for stage testing of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket. This commercial partnership supports NASA’s goal of landing American astronauts on the Moon and building a Moon Base. His daily responsibilities include ensuring facility electronics are operational to collect accurate data, running conduit and cabling, connecting data-collecting instruments, and verifying that motor valves operate as intended.

The move to civil servant status has increased Spiers’ sense of ownership and pride in his work. Although he noted that he was never treated differently while a contractor, he feels more integrated into the team as a civil servant. This family-oriented mindset extends to his personal life, where his father, Joey Spiers, also transitioned from a longtime contractor to a civil servant in the summer of 2026 and works as an electrical engineering technician. Additionally, Spiers’ brother-in-law, Brock Sheppard, joined NASA as a mechanical engineering technician in September 2026.

Spiers actively mentors others and shares his professional journey with the community. During NASA’s Career Technical Education Day at Stennis in September 2026, he spoke to community college students and a virtual audience of thousands about his path to NASA, the importance of a strong work ethic, and how technical skills contribute to the agency’s mission. He credits veteran employees who mentored him early in his career for his current success and views his current crew as extended family.
summary: Jared Spiers, an electrical engineering technician at NASA’s Stennis Space Center, transitioned from a contractor to a civil servant in June 2026. He is currently part of the team preparing the Thad Cochran Test Stand for stage testing of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket.
author: NASA News

title: Hubble Image of Gravitational Lens Preps NASA's Roman Space Telescope
content:
NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope captured a sweeping barred galaxy in the center of an image taken on Oct. 22, 2026, with a vivid gravitational lens appearing in the bottom‑right corner. The picture was produced by NASA, ESA, and X. Huang of the University of San Francisco, and processed by Gladys Kober of NASA/Catholic University of America.

This observation is one of many gravitational‑lensing images collected by Hubble in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope. Astronomers plan to use these images to analyze gravitational distortions, learn more about dark matter in the foreground galaxies, and lay the groundwork for future Roman observations.

The images illustrate how Hubble and Roman will work together to build a more comprehensive picture of the cosmos, as noted by the image credit to NASA, ESA, and X. Huang, with processing by Gladys Kober.
summary: Hubble captured a sinuous spiral galaxy and a vivid gravitational lens in the same field of view on Oct. 22, 2026. The image is part of a series of gravitational lensing observations that will help astronomers study dark matter and prepare for future Roman Space Telescope observations.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Releases 2026 ISAM State of Play, 368‑Page Industry Standard for Space Servicing
content:
NASA’s Langley Research Center has released the 2026 edition of the In-Space Servicing, Assembly, and Manufacturing (ISAM) State of Play, a comprehensive document that has evolved into a primary industry resource. Dale Arney, senior team lead for the ISAM Technology Portfolio at NASA Langley, noted that the team recognized an inflection point when companies began requesting access to the report for competitive intelligence. Although some unnamed companies inquired about proprietary information, Arney confirmed that the document contains no such data. This impartiality is cited as a key factor in the report’s value to an industry seeking to understand a rapidly expanding field.

Published annually since 2021, the 2026 edition has expanded to 368 pages and documents current capabilities across 11 functional areas, including robotic manipulation, refueling, and structural assembly. The cover of the document features Astronaut F. Story Musgrave, who anchored on the Space Shuttle Endeavor’s robotic arm during the 1993 servicing mission of the Hubble Space Telescope. Arney described the field as having expanded more than linearly since the report’s inception. What started as a tool to ensure NASA centers shared a common reference point has become the industry’s go-to resource for distinguishing between what is currently possible and what remains conceptual.

The ISAM State of Play team enforces strict entry criteria for inclusion, requiring that hardware physically exist as either ground prototypes or in-flight demonstrations. Arney stated that the team rejects submissions consisting solely of PowerPoint presentations of technology ideas without evidence of actual work. Concepts that do not meet these hardware requirements are deferred until the following year’s review. This rigor is considered essential because ISAM capabilities are intended to enable missions that are impossible with traditional single-launch approaches, such as telescopes larger than any launch vehicle fairing, mobile national security assets, and commercial systems capable of on-orbit upgrades without full replacement.

John Mulvaney, a team member, described the document as a "crowdsource document" that relies on annual interviews with industry partners to ensure accuracy and completeness. Contributions to the report come from various NASA centers, including Ames, Glenn, Marshall, Kennedy, and Johnson, as well as international developers who meet the hardware criteria. The 2026 edition includes developer profiles and facilities documentation, providing mission designers with information on who is performing the work and where the facilities are located. This collaborative approach aims to offer both competitive context and collaboration opportunities for companies entering or expanding within the ISAM ecosystem.

The report serves as a technical reference and a roadmap for technologies that enable spacecraft to be serviced, assembled, and manufactured in orbit rather than launched as integrated systems. As the space industry moves toward more ambitious missions, including lunar infrastructure and on-orbit manufacturing, the ISAM State of Play provides a shared vocabulary and capability baseline. Arney emphasized that the document is not speculation about the future but rather documentation of what exists now and where the hardware is heading next. The 2026 ISAM State of Play is available for download at NASA.gov.
summary: NASA Releases 2026 ISAM State of Play, 368‑Page Industry Standard for Space Servicing.
author: NASA News

title: NASA invites public to send names on microchip aboard Dragonfly mission to Titan
content: The “Journey to Titan” campaign offers the public the opportunity to fly their names on a microchip with NASA’s Dragonfly mission. The chip will ride aboard the Dragonfly rotorcraft as it explores Saturn’s moon Titan by air. Credit: NASA/Johns Hopkins APL You may never soar under the clouds or over the organic sands of Saturn’s moon Titan, but your name can. NASA is inviting the public to send their names aboard the agency’s Dragonfly rotorcraft and be part of the first science mission to fly and explore the surface of another world. To have your name included on a microchip aboard Dragonfly and receive a personalized digital boarding pass commemorating your place on this historic mission, visit: https://go. Nasa. Gov/dragonfly-names “NASA’s Dragonfly mission will simply blow your mind,” said Nicky Fox, associate administrator, Science Mission Directorate, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By flying the first-ever rotorcraft science mission, NASA will explore Saturn’s largest moon, Titan, as we search for signs of habitability on a distant world that is most similar to our own. We are excited to bring humanity along for the journey of a lifetime, and we invite everyone to send their names on this small, but mighty rotorcraft that will unlock the secrets of the universe in what is widely considered one of the most exciting space missions of our lifetime.” The public can secure a place on Dragonfly’s passenger list until 11:59 p. M. EST Jan. 15, 2027. The Dragonfly rotorcraft is currently being assembled at the Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland. Scheduled to launch in 2028, the rotorcraft will travel to Titan, a remarkable world with a thick atmosphere, rivers and lakes of liquid methane, sweeping dunes, and a landscape rich in organic material. After arriving in 2034, Dragonfly will fly to different locations on the moon, exploring Titan’s diverse environments and searching for clues about prebiotic chemistry — the chemistry that came before biology — to help scientists better understand the ingredients and conditions for life. Dragonfly is being designed and built under the direction of APL, which leads the mission for NASA. Elizabeth Turtle of APL is the principal investigator. Dragonfly is the fourth mission in NASA’s New Frontiers Program, managed by NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center in Huntsville, Alabama, for the agency’s Science Mission Directorate. For more information on NASA’s Dragonfly mission, visit: https://science. Nasa. Gov/mission/dragonfly/ -end- Karen Fox / Molly Wasser Headquarters, Washington 240-285-5155 / 240-419-1732 karen. C. Fox@nasa. Gov / molly. L. Wasser@nasa. Gov Mike Buckley Johns Hopkins Applied Physics Laboratory 443-567-3145 michael. Buckley@jhuapl. Edu Share Details Last Updated Oct 29, 2026 Editor Jessica Taveau Location NASA Headquarters Related Terms Dragonfly Marshall Space Flight Center Saturn Saturn Moons Science Mission Directorate Titan
summary: The “Journey to Titan” campaign offers the public the opportunity to fly their names on a microchip with NASA’s Dragonfly mission. The chip will ride aboard the Dragonfly rotorcraft as it explores Saturn’s moon Titan by air.
author: NASA News

title: Snap’s $2,195 Specs Hold During Push-Ups, Still Feel Like Prototype
content: The author tested Snap’s Specs AR glasses while doing push‑ups, noting that they fit better than their bulky appearance suggests and remain secure during movement. Despite this, the $2,195 device still feels like a developer prototype searching for a clear purpose.
summary: The author performed push-ups wearing Snap’s $2,195 Specs, which fit better than they look and stay put during movement. Despite this, the glasses still feel like a developer prototype searching for a purpose.
author: Wired

title: Hacker Uses Malware to Reveal Cards of High‑Stakes Poker Players
content: Illicit software was installed on the computers of several of the world’s top online poker players. The malware enabled the accused cheater to view the cards in the victims’ hands, allowing him to beat them at the tables.
summary: Illicit software on the computers of some of the world’s best online poker players allowed the accused cheater to see what cards were in the victims’ hands. The cheater then trounced them at the tables.

title: NYT Cooking tests AI feature to modify recipes
content:
The New York Times is testing a new artificial‑intelligence feature for its Cooking app, a move announced by NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko last Friday. The update is designed to help users modify recipes on the fly and has already sparked some drama among the app’s community.

The AI tool offers a range of recipe‑adjustment options. It can recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and, according to Ko, “generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment.” These capabilities aim to make the app’s recipes more flexible for everyday cooking.

An example highlighted in the announcement shows a user asking to replace kale with baby spinach. The app explained that baby spinach wilts faster and suggested adding it during a later step of the recipe.
summary: The New York Times is testing an AI feature in its Cooking app that recommends ingredient substitutions, scales servings, and adjusts recipe steps. Senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature last Friday, and it advises users to add baby spinach later in a recipe when replacing kale because the spinach wilts faster.

content:

It traces the company’s history over the past quarter‑century, noting that Elon Musk and his chief operating officer, Gwynne Shotwell, have long viewed the United States government as “El Dorado,” a mythical source of contracts. The piece describes how the duo navigated a competitive landscape that included Boeing and Lockheed Martin, as well as regulatory and financial obstacles.  

According to the article, Musk and Shotwell sued when disputes arose, voiced concerns about an uneven playing field, and ultimately delivered space products to the U.S. government at lower costs. Their efforts secured a steady stream of contracts, allowing SpaceX to thrive independently of NASA.
summary: SpaceX's Independence from NASA Raises Concerns for U.S. Space Agency.

title: 41,000 DHS employees and contractors exposed in massive data leak
content:
A large data breach has revealed the identities of more than 41,000 employees or contractors who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and its component agencies. The leaked files contain email addresses, phone numbers, office addresses, and references to internal systems, as well as sensitive information about undercover and surveillance programs. The data provides a detailed map of DHS’s organizational structure and operational procedures.

The records cover DHS itself and seven of its component agencies, including Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). They were last updated on August 19, 2026.

The archive, titled “Icepick,” was published by the transparency nonprofit Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets) on Wednesday. Cybersecurity researcher and journalist maia arson crimew previewed the data for WIRED, saying it was obtained from a group that calls itself the Department of Peace. DDoSecrets stated that the data came from DHS’s Okta login system, and the hackers included a note that read, “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs.”
summary: An unprecedented leak of Department of Homeland Security records exposed details of more than 41,000 employees or contractors, including email addresses, phone numbers, and office addresses. The leak, released by DDoSecrets as “Icepick,” was sourced from DHS's Okta login system and includes references to internal systems and undercover surveillance programs.

title: Night Plane review: indie horror game puts players on a doomed jumbo jet
content: Liquid Static Studio; PC You take on the role of flight attendant in this clever and absorbing retro-style game that veers from daft horror spoof to genuinely disturbing There was always something creepy about the job-simulator genre. All those mindless automatons queueing up to use your bus, bar or bed store, or whatever workplace you are trapped in for the duration of the game. The endless repetitive tasks. The emptiness of the world beyond your corporate existence. Together, these elements scream existential terror … which is perhaps why we are now seeing a new indie sub-genre of job sim horror games, including Home Safety Hotline, Dredge and more recently, Grease Trap ’99, a Lovecraftian mystery set in a Scottish chip shop. Now, we have Night Plane, in which you take on the role of a flight attendant on a jumbo jet to hell. It all starts kind of normally. You turn up for the first day of your new job, meet your colleagues, then take your spot at the departure gate, checking in customers and being careful to root out anyone with invalid tickets. Once on the plane, you roll your trolley down the aisle, serving booze and inedible meals, and occasionally dealing with passenger complaints. Then the plane crashes and, frankly, it all goes downhill from there.
summary: Night Plane is a retro‑style PC game by Liquid Static Studio that lets you play as a flight attendant on a jumbo jet. The game begins with routine duties such as checking tickets and serving passengers before the plane crashes and the experience becomes disturbing.

After four and a half years of parenting two small kids, she describes a day spent inside as a greater challenge than navigating the front door on a rainy morning. She adds that being outside benefits her mental health and that routine outings—like a bus ride or a doctor’s visit—naturally provide sensory stimulation and ideas for role‑play activities.

title: Spain declares three days of mourning after high‑speed rail collision kills 69
content:
Spain has declared a three‑day period of mourning after a high‑speed rail collision claimed 69 lives. Emergency services, drones and a police dog unit are continuing to search the wreckage, while the Civil Guard has established clinics where relatives can provide DNA samples.

The accident involved two trains traveling on the same line from Madrid toward Andalucía. One was operated by the state‑owned Renfe and the other by the private company Iryo. Shortly before 9 a.m., the Iryo train stopped near the town of Urda in Castilla‑La Mancha, and the Renfe train struck its rear, knocking several carriages off the track.

Hospitals are treating dozens of injured passengers as families await news about their loved ones. The search and identification effort remains ongoing.

title: Spain high‑speed train crash near Toledo kills at least 69, investigators probe signalling
content:
At least 69 people died when a high‑speed Renfe AVE train traveling from Madrid to Seville collided with an Iryo train on the same track near Toledo on Wednesday morning. Both trains had been stopped earlier after a signalling system failure; controllers later instructed the AVE driver to restart the journey, after which the AVE train struck the Iryo train from behind. The impact destroyed the AVE’s front carriages and the Iryo train’s rear, and caused additional derailing.

Investigators will examine the audio file that appears to implicate the control centre, as well as the signalling failure and other technical issues surrounding the restart order. Their inquiry will focus on why the AVE driver was told to proceed and how the signalling system malfunction contributed to the crash.
summary: At least 69 people died when a state‑owned Renfe AVE train from Madrid to Seville collided with a private Iryo train on the same track near Toledo on Wednesday morning after both were halted by a signalling failure. Investigators will question the control centre’s restart order, the signalling system and possible technical problems.

title: Rare letters from La Pérouse expedition reveal Louis XVI's 1793 inquiry about missing navigator
content:
A recent discovery of a “miracle” cache of letters written by a French scientist who perished in the ill‑fated La Pérouse mission has provided a personal account of the 1785 round‑the‑world voyage. The letters, now preserved, offer firsthand details of the expedition’s scientific objectives and daily life aboard the ships that were sent to rival the discoveries of English explorer Captain James Cook.

In the same historical context, the French king, Louis XVI, is reported to have asked, “Is there news of Monsieur de la Pérouse?” as he prepared to climb the scaffolding for his public execution by guillotine on 21 January 1793. The question referred to Jean‑François de Galaup, the Count of Pérouse, a naval officer and navigator who had been dispatched in 1785 on a global scientific mission.
summary: Rare letters from La Pérouse expedition reveal Louis XVI's 1793 inquiry about missing navigator.
author: Guardian World

title: Lawyers for Marist Brothers subpoenaed over advice to keep child abuser out of legal arena
content: A once-confidential letter says child sexual abuser might implicate senior church officials if allowed near ‘the legal arena’ upon his release from jail Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Lawyers from a leading law firm for the Marist Brothers have been subpoenaed to explain a once-confidential document showing they advised the Catholic order to keep a serial offender out of “the legal arena”, suggesting he was too honest and might implicate senior church officials. The offender was “regrettably up front” about his interactions with senior leadership, and could not be trusted to heed “suggestions” about “not dumping on others excessively”, the document says.
summary: Lawyers from a leading law firm representing the Marist Brothers were subpoenaed to explain a once‑confidential document. The document advised the Catholic order to keep a serial child sexual abuser out of “the legal arena” because he might implicate senior church officials.
author: Guardian World

title: Erin Patterson's appeal decision to determine possible retrial or longer sentence
content:
Erin Patterson will learn on Friday whether the Victorian Court of Appeal will impose a longer prison term or order a new trial in her triple‑murder case. The court, Victoria’s highest appellate body, is scheduled to deliver its ruling from 10 a.m. after hearing the two appeals.

Justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from Patterson’s legal team and prosecutors in August and will now determine the outcome of the appeals. The decision will address whether Patterson faces a retrial, a longer sentence, or both.
summary: Victoria’s Court of Appeal will deliver its decision on Friday on two appeals in Erin Patterson’s triple‑murder case, determining whether she faces a longer prison term or a new trial. The panel of Justices Lesley Taylor, Stephen McLeish and Peter Kidd heard arguments from her lawyers and prosecutors in August.
author: Guardian World

title: Study of 100,000 Australians seeks causes of mental health disorders and early onset cancer
content:
The Sax Institute has launched the 18 and Up study, an intergenerational research project that will follow the health of Australians aged 18 to 45 over the course of their lives. The independent, not‑for‑profit institute is recruiting 100,000 participants to become part of Australia’s largest study of wellbeing and ageing.

Researchers hope the data will help identify the drivers of major health challenges that affect younger people, including mental illness and rising cancer rates. By tracking participants over time, the study aims to uncover early risk factors and improve prevention strategies for mental health disorders and early‑onset cancer.
summary: Study of 100,000 Australians seeks causes of mental health disorders and early onset cancer.
author: Guardian World

title: Stephen Graham stars as serial killer Jurek Walter in new thriller Nocturne
content:
Stephen Graham stars as Jurek Walter, a sadistic serial killer, in the new 10-part psychological thriller Nocturne. The character is incarcerated for life in the basement of the Riverside psychiatric hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Walter is depicted as a murderer who tortures both his victims and their families, utilizing a high-pitched giggle and fatal whispers to drive fellow inmates to suicide by communicating through the pipes. The review notes that Graham, described as muscle-bound and preternaturally still, delivers a mesmerizing and terrifying performance.

The article suggests that Graham may have surpassed Anthony Hopkins as the screen’s most profoundly unsettling serial killer, a status previously held by the actor from Hannibal. Walter is shown passing his time in confinement by doing push-ups and stashing contraband behind his toilet bowl for unspecified purposes. The review characterizes the series as a perfectly terrifying show suitable for Halloween, highlighting the difficulty of looking away from Graham’s portrayal of the character.
summary: Stephen Graham plays Jurek Walter, a sadistic murderer incarcerated at Riverside psychiatric hospital in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. The character manipulates fellow inmates and tortures victims' families in the new 10-part psychological thriller.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Documentary explores Sylvester Stallone's creation of Rocky
content:
To mark the fiftieth anniversary of Rocky, a new film explores the life of Sylvester Stallone, highlighting his personal struggles before the movie’s release. The article notes that Stallone was belittled for his speech and appearance and was so financially strained that he sold his dog. Despite these hardships, he wrote and starred in the boxing film, which depicts a Philadelphia underdog who fights the world heavyweight champion to the final bell.

The creation of the film is described as an underdog story in itself, as the out-of-work character actor convinced a studio to finance the project and cast him in the title role. Stallone surpassed his fictional character by winning the best picture Oscar. The text emphasizes the enduring impact of the franchise, noting that thousands of people still climb the 72 steps of the Philadelphia Museum of Art annually to pay homage to the character.
summary: The article discusses how out-of-work actor Sylvester Stallone wrote and starred in the 1976 film Rocky. It highlights the movie's status as an underdog story that won a best picture Oscar and remains a cultural landmark.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Writers face surge in fake literary scams targeting aspiring authors
content:
Writers are increasingly targeted by a surge in literary scams, receiving daily invitations from fake book groups and offers to publicize their work. The article highlights how aspiring authors are often vulnerable to these fraudulent schemes. One specific example involves author Snigdha Poonam, who received an email from a man claiming to be Timothy Firth, the organizer of a Seattle-based life-drawing community called CAM Life Drawing.

The email addressed Poonam as “Professor” and claimed the group wanted to discuss her book, Dreamers: How Young Indians Are Changing Their World, at an upcoming meetup. Attendees were reportedly encouraged to leave reviews on Goodreads and Amazon afterward. Although Poonam found an events page and an Instagram account for the group, which featured photos and testimonials of a white male named Timothy Firth, she suspected the sender was not the genuine organizer. The piece questions who is behind this explosion in literary fraud.
summary: Writers are increasingly receiving daily invitations from fake book groups and offers to publicise their work. The article details a specific scam involving a fake organizer named Timothy Firth who contacted an author to discuss her book.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Mid-century modern furniture loses favor with millennials, says Norfolk dealer
content: Once coveted for its clean lines and timeless design, the functional furniture is no longer seen as cool. Anyone for cottagecore and chrome? “I definitely don’t think it is cringe,” says Laura Budds, a vintage furniture dealer based in Norfolk. “But I do think we have reached the peak, and we’re on the descent.” Budds is talking about mid-century modern furniture, which has recently come under fire from younger generations for being – like so many things, including trainer socks and high-waisted jeans – a deeply millennial aesthetic. As the Wall Street Journal declared : “Midcentury modern design has met the fate of pumpkin spice lattes, cocktails in mason jars, no-show socks, leggings and other aspects of millennial culture: it has become cringey.” Budds, 44, is resigned to the fact that she is a “mid-century millennial”. She’s even made a career out of it: she sells furniture and vintage clothes at Williams & Parfitt, a modern antiques centre in Wymondham, Norfolk. But she says she has had to diversify in recent years to cater to changing tastes among younger customers, who are moving away from the “wall-to-wall mid-century” look beloved by the generation above them. She says of gen Z: “I don’t think they are so bound by the eras or designers – they just buy what they like. They aren’t afraid of older antiques and will have a bit of whimsy or taxidermy.”
summary: Laura Budds, a 44‑year‑old vintage furniture dealer in Norfolk, says mid‑century modern furniture has peaked and is now viewed as cringey by younger generations. She has diversified her offerings at Williams & Parfitt in Wymondham as Gen Z shoppers move away from the “wall‑to‑wall mid‑century” look.
author: Guardian Culture

title: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down
content:
A three-year-old boy from Florida gained significant attention after a video of his soccer skills went viral. In the footage, the toddler is shown running end-to-end and scoring multiple goals against opponents who appear to be just learning the game. The child’s father, identified as the cameraman, is seen loudly cheering his son on during the match. The story also involves a claim by the parents that police were called to the scene to stop opposing defenders who could not tackle the child.

Police records reviewed by the Guardian have complicated this narrative, raising troubling questions about the situation. The article notes that the internet broadly embraced the toddler, with references to figures like Ms. Rachel and Roc Nation. However, the piece argues that the actual tragedy is broader than the initial outrage cycle suggests, implicating more people and presenting a more depressing reality than the viral moment implies.
summary: A three-year-old soccer prodigy went viral. The adults have already let him down.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Tottenham's 2-0 win at Chelsea ends 34-match Premier League winless streak
content:
Tottenham Hotspur’s Premier League campaign has gained momentum following a 2-0 victory over Chelsea last Saturday. This result provided a significant boost to their standing in the table, marking a notable turnaround from their poor start to the season. The win is considered particularly substantial because it was a clean sheet at Stamford Bridge, a feat Tottenham had not achieved in any competition since December 1986.

The victory also broke a long-standing historical trend. Prior to this match, Tottenham had won only once in their previous 34 visits to Chelsea in the Premier League. That last win occurred in April 2018 under manager Mauricio Pochettino, a period when the team was described as a formidable force. For many supporters, this recent success represents a rare occurrence that has only been witnessed once before in their recent memory.
summary: Tottenham secured their first Premier League victory at Chelsea in 34 attempts with a 2-0 win. This result was also their first clean sheet at Stamford Bridge in any competition since December 1986.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Milwaukee Brewers close out Tampa Bay Rays to end 57-year wait for first World Series title
content:
The Milwaukee Brewers secured their first World Series title on Wednesday by defeating the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5, completing a four-games-to-one victory. This championship ends a 57-year wait for the franchise’s first baseball prize. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt contributed two runs batted in, while Jacob Misiorowski pitched five and two-thirds scoreless innings in the decisive game.

Miguel Contreras was named the World Series MVP after batting .381 during the series. The victory marks the culmination of a season that began in spring training with championship ambitions, resulting in the first title in the franchise’s 58th year.
summary: Milwaukee Brewers close out Tampa Bay Rays to end 57-year wait for first World Series title.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Everton face Newcastle in Carabao Cup as owners seek sale
content:
Everton manager David Moyes faces a challenging backdrop as his team prepares for a Carabao Cup fourth-round match against Newcastle United at Hill Dickinson Stadium. The club’s owners, The Friedkin Group, have halted squad investment and announced plans to sell the team, a shift that contrasts with the season’s initial goals of European qualification and ending a trophy drought. Despite these changes in ownership direction and reduced resources, the demands on Moyes remain unchanged as he seeks to maintain the team’s competitive standards.

The upcoming match offers a specific opportunity for Everton to advance in a competition they have never won, potentially fulfilling one of their stated campaign objectives. The game is also seen as a chance to restore team morale following consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal, which are the only losses Everton has recorded this season. Newcastle fans will be present in significant numbers, with 7,732 supporters attending after Everton allocated 15% of the stadium capacity to their opponents.
summary: The Friedkin Group announced they are looking to sell Everton and have stopped squad investment, yet David Moyes must still pursue a trophy drought that will soon reach 32 years. Everton plays Newcastle in the Carabao Cup fourth round to restore positivity after consecutive defeats against Chelsea and Arsenal.

content: England began their final group match of the men’s cricket tri-series in Lahore against Sri Lanka, with the first over recorded at 0-0. title: ‘I’m no special guy. We can all do this’: Loek Hartog on rescuing Ollie Millroy from a burning car
content: Last month in Shanghai, the Dutch driver saved Ollie Millroy’s life after a crash. The incident created a unique friendship and a shared determination to improve safety Winter is coming and, at eight in the morning, Amsterdam is dark as Loek Hartog and I walk towards the park. The GT motor racing driver is only 24 but, after all he did last month, when he showed extraordinary courage in saving the life of his fellow racer Ollie Millroy, we talk easily about life and death. Hartog sips a takeaway coffee and, as we stroll, he asks if the world seems to be in a worse state than usual. Paris is burning, Kyiv is reeling, Vladimir Putin is being hailed as “a humanitarian” by Donald Trump’s envoy and the robots are coming for us. These are grim times, but I remind Hartog that he gave us hope as, after ripping off the doors of Millroy’s burning car as if he had stepped out of a superhero movie, his humanity was remarkably moving. Hartog dragged Millroy to safety before trying to comfort the 36-year-old Briton after an accident that left him with six broken ribs, a damaged lung, a splintered collarbone, a broken hand, a fractured C6 neck vertebrae and a stunned sense that he had almost died at the China GT.
summary: Last month in Shanghai, the Dutch driver saved Ollie Millroy’s life after a crash. The incident created a unique friendship and a shared determination to improve safety Winter is coming and, at eight in the morning, Amsterdam is dark as Loek Hartog and I walk towards the park.

content:
Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets) released a dataset on Wednesday that lists more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including some who work in the intelligence community.  

The collective did not name the source of the personnel information; instead, it referred to the unnamed individual as the “Department of Peace.”
summary: DDoSecrets released a dataset containing information on over 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including some intelligence community staff. The leaker was unnamed and referred to as the “Department of Peace.”

content: A new Marquette University Law School Poll released Wednesday shows Democrat David Crowley leading Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany (R‑Wis.) by 51 percent to 44 percent of likely Wisconsin voters, a 7‑point margin that represents a 2‑point increase from last month’s poll. The results indicate Crowley has slightly widened his advantage in the state’s gubernatorial race.
summary: Democrat David Crowley has slightly widened his lead over his GOP opponent, Rep. Tom Tiffany (R-Wis.), in Wisconsin’s gubernatorial contest, according to new polling released Wednesday.

content:

He declared the scheme “voter fraud at the highest level” while rallying in Chillicothe.
summary: President Trump criticized Senate Democrats and former Rep. content: Former President Barack Obama criticized Republicans for prioritizing a joke over economic concerns. At a campaign rally in Georgia on Wednesday, he said the White House had “mobilized a whole‑of‑government response to that joke, not to inflation, but to that joke,” after a recent campaign‑trail jab at President Trump’s White House decorations.

content: Hacktivists known as Distributed Denial of Secrets claim to have exposed the identities of over 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including ICE agents, operatives, and contractors. The group justified the unmasking as fair play, citing the government’s lack of transparency.
summary: Hacktivists known as Distributed Denial of Secrets claim that exposing the identities of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors is justified by the government's lack of transparency. They argue that the unmasking is fair play.

title: Labour MPs urge PM, Chancellor not to overrule Energy Secretary over Rosebank oilfield decision
content: Furious Labour backbenchers are lobbying the Prime Minister and Chancellor to avoid overruling Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh regarding the Rosebank oilfield. The MPs expressed alarm over emerging cabinet splits, stating that Fahnbulleh faces an “intolerable position” if she is forced to change her stance. summary: Labour MPs have been lobbying the prime minister and chancellor not to overrule Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh if she blocks the Rosebank oilfield. They are alarmed at cabinet splits after sources told the Guardian that Fahnbulleh may refuse environmental permission for the field.

title: Roswell Park study shows bevacizumab and pazopanib extend survival in kidney cancer
content: A phase 1/2 trial led by Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center found that combining targeted therapies bevacizumab (Avastin) and pazopanib (Votrient) significantly extends progression-free and overall survival in patients with the most common type of kidney cancer. Saby George, M. D., FACP, professor of oncology in the Department of Medicine, served as the principal investigator and first author of the study. The research findings were newly published in The Lancet Oncology.
summary: Results of a phase 1/2 trial led by Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center show that combining the targeted therapies bevacizumab (Avastin) and pazopanib (Votrient) significantly extends both progression-free and overall survival in patients with the most common type of kidney cancer. title: Buttock shape does not indicate estrogen levels, contrary to social media claims
content: Recent social media posts claim that buttock shape indicates estrogen levels, but experts state this is inaccurate. The shape of the bottom does not reveal hormone levels, and determining them requires appropriate laboratory testing rather than physical appearance.
summary: The shape of your bottom cannot tell you anything about your hormones, despite recent social media posts. Determining hormone levels requires appropriate laboratory testing, as buttock shape is not a reliable indicator.

title: More than 120,000 Americans living with acute lymphoblastic leukemia
content:
A new lab‑on‑a‑chip platform has been developed that can predict which cancer treatments may be effective for pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). The technology is designed to help clinicians identify the most promising therapies for children diagnosed with this aggressive blood cancer.  

In the United States, more than 120,000 people live with ALL, and about 6,000 new cases are diagnosed each year. Of those new cases, more than 3,500 involve children. ALL accounts for 75 % of all pediatric leukemia diagnoses and is a rapid‑onset blood cancer that can prevent the body from producing mature, infection‑fighting white blood cells within months.
summary: More than 120,000 Americans living with acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

title: Waterloo researchers find tiny eye bumps linked to Fuchs corneal dystrophy
content:
University of Waterloo researchers discovered that tiny bumps inside the eye contribute to Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), a disease that can cause severe vision loss.  

Because donated corneas are scarce worldwide, the finding may lead to alternative treatment strategies and reduce the need for corneal transplants in some patients.
summary: University of Waterloo researchers discovered that tiny bumps inside the eye contribute to Fuchs endothelial corneal dystrophy (FECD), an eye disease that can cause severe vision loss. The finding could lead to alternative treatment strategies and reduce the need for corneal transplants in some patients.

title: UC researchers develop HeartBot AI chatbot to help women recognize heart disease
content:
HeartBot, a chatbot developed by a team of UC researchers, routinely answers questions from women who are looking for information about heart disease. The program is designed to provide quick, accessible guidance on heart‑health topics.

The project was led by Yoshimi Fukuoka, Ph. D., RN, FAAN, a nurse scientist and professor at UC San Francisco’s School of Nursing. Its aim is to determine whether giving study participants a heart‑health chatbot on their phone increases their awareness of heart‑disease risks and improves their ability to recognize heart‑attack symptoms, encouraging timely medical help when needed.

title: Immune changes linked to diabetes could guide development of new cancer treatments
content:
A new study published in The Journal of Immunology suggests that high blood sugar and type 1 diabetes (T1D) may protect against certain cancers, including melanoma, breast and colon cancer. Researchers have long noted a lower risk of these cancers among people with T1D, but the underlying mechanism has been unclear.

Recent experiments in mice indicate that hyperglycemia induces changes in immune cells called T cells, which could explain the reduced cancer risk observed in individuals with T1D.
summary: New research in The Journal of Immunology shows that high blood sugar and type 1 diabetes may protect against cancers such as melanoma, breast, and colon cancer. The study in mice suggests that this protection may result from changes in T cells caused by hyperglycemia.

content: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have created a low‑cost method to convert the tiny packages cells naturally exchange into drug carriers. By attaching customizable DNA labels, these carriers can be directed specifically to cancer cells, a strategy intended to boost treatment effectiveness while lowering side effects.
summary: Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have developed a simple, low‑cost method that converts natural cellular packages into drug carriers. The customizable DNA labels guide these carriers to deliver treatments directly to cancer cells, which could improve effectiveness and reduce side effects.

title: New tissue atlas aims to help AI understand cancer
content:
A new tissue atlas has been developed to aid artificial‑intelligence systems in understanding cancer. The atlas focuses on how cells are arranged within tissues, a factor that can reveal as much about disease as the cells themselves.

When doctors examine a cancer tumor, they assess not only which cells are present but also how those cells are positioned and how they interact with one another. The arrangement and interaction of cancer cells with neighboring immune cells can provide important clues about how the disease develops or how it may respond to treatment.
summary: The arrangement of cells within tissue provides significant insights into disease, similar to the cells themselves. In cancer, the interaction between tumor cells and neighboring immune cells offers clues about disease development and treatment response.
