title: MIT Researchers Launch Social.Wiki, Let Users Edit Social Apps Without Coding
content:
MIT researchers have unveiled Social.Wiki, a platform that lets users edit and customize social applications directly within the web ecosystem. The system was developed in response to user frustration over changes made to popular messaging platforms—such as the addition of an AI chatbot—that users could not alter without leaving the service. Social.Wiki gives users the ability to modify any social application created on the platform and to choose which edits made by others they wish to see.

Each Social.Wiki site includes an “edit” button that opens a page where users can view and change the site’s source code or prompt an AI assistant to make adjustments. The platform is built on a decentralized infrastructure, meaning no single machine owns a website or its underlying infrastructure. User data are stored separately from the sites that access them, and a “data guard” prompts users to review each request for data access, ensuring that users remain in control of their information. Social.Wiki also implements a plural governance model: users can set rules that determine which edits they will see, and can designate “trusted editors” whose changes are automatically accepted.

The research team, led by Theia Henderson, an EECS graduate student at MIT, and senior author David Karger, a professor of EECS and member of CSAIL, published a paper that will be presented at the ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology in November. Other authors include EECS graduate students Carmel Schare and Ana Dodik, Professor Clemens Klokmose of Aarhus University, postdoc Ziv Epstein of the MIT Media Lab, and research scientist David D. Clark.

Case studies demonstrate the breadth of applications that can be built on Social.Wiki, ranging from a messaging platform that allows styling changes without affecting others, to a rideshare app with a dynamic pricing algorithm and a collaborative canvas for shared art. The team also ran a hackathon where participants created a housing co‑op communication tool and a garden‑themed microblogging site. Moving forward, the researchers plan to deploy Social.Wiki to a wider audience, add end‑to‑end encryption for private messages, and improve developer tools. The work received partial funding from Schmidt Sciences and the National Science Foundation.
summary: MIT researchers created Social.Wiki, a decentralized platform that lets users edit social applications and choose which edits to see without needing coding skills. The system includes a data guard to protect user data and allows users to set governance policies to control which edits are displayed.
author: MIT News

title: Scientists find magma can store extra oxygen, hinting at hidden atmospheric contributor
content:
Scientists have discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen, potentially revealing a hidden contributor to Earth’s oxygen‑rich atmosphere.  

The findings suggest that ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth’s atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.
summary: Scientists discovered that magma deep inside Earth can store surprising amounts of extra oxygen. The findings suggest ancient volcanic eruptions may have helped transform Earth's atmosphere billions of years ago, with implications for understanding life on other planets.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists identify seven stages of meteoroid breakup, showing melting and fragmentation
content: Scientists have uncovered seven surprising stages that space rocks go through as they hurtle toward Earth, revealing that melting and violent fragmentation, rather than simple evaporation, determine their fate. The discovery could help explain why meteorites scatter across the ground and how dangerous asteroids explode in Earth's atmosphere.
summary: Scientists have uncovered seven surprising stages that space rocks go through as they hurtle toward Earth, revealing that melting and violent fragmentation, rather than simple evaporation, determine their fate. The discovery could help explain why meteorites scatter across the ground and how dangerous asteroids explode in Earth's atmosphere.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists generate X‑rays beyond laser physics limit using paired electrons
content: Scientists have defied a long‑standing rule of laser physics by generating X‑rays with energies far higher than conventional theory predicts. The finding shows that two electrons working together can surpass a previously accepted limit, potentially opening new avenues for quantum research.
summary: Scientists have defied a long‑standing rule of laser physics by generating X‑rays with energies higher than conventional theory predicts. The discovery shows that two electrons working together can overcome the previously accepted limit, opening new possibilities for quantum research.
author: Science Daily

title: Your blood pressure could be dangerous even when your numbers look normal
content: Researchers have identified a small cluster of brain cells that suppress hazardous blood‑pressure fluctuations even when average measurements seem normal. The discovery points to a concealed source of cardiovascular risk and suggests the possibility of new therapies aimed at safeguarding the heart and brain.
summary: Researchers have discovered a small group of brain cells that prevents dangerous blood pressure swings, even when average readings appear normal. The finding reveals a hidden source of cardiovascular risk and could open the door to new treatments that protect the heart and brain.
author: Science Daily

title: Terry Tao's plant coin puzzle and solution shared
content: Earlier today a puzzle originally posed by UCLA professor Terry Tao was posted, and the author has now republished it together with its solutions. The problem describes two types of plants: a regular plant that yields one coin each day, and a mother plant that yields one coin and two seeds daily. Each seed matures into a regular plant on the following day. The updated post includes the complete solution to this mathematical puzzle.
summary: Earlier today a puzzle by UCLA professor Terry Tao was posted and solutions were provided. The puzzle describes a regular plant that produces one coin per day and a mother plant that produces one coin and two seeds per day, with each seed becoming a regular plant the following day.
author: Guardian Science

title: Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman appointed Caltech associate VP and JPL deputy director
content: 4 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) Former NASA astronaut and Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman joins Caltech and NASA JPL as Caltech associate vice president and JPL deputy director on Nov. 30. Photo Credit: NASA Artemis II Commander Reid Wiseman has been named Caltech associate vice president and deputy director of NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The emeritus astronaut and retired U. S. Navy captain begins his new role at NASA’s center of excellence for robotics and deep space exploration and at Caltech, which manages JPL for NASA, on Nov. 30, 2026. “Reid has spent his career at the edge of what is possible, and he has the technical judgment, operational experience, and leadership to help push that edge farther,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “As commander of Artemis II, he helped carry America back around the Moon, and now, as an emeritus astronaut, he will continue giving back to NASA from a new vantage point at JPL. Reid is joining a storied laboratory that has made an enormous amount of history, and there is a lot more ahead. I am excited to see what he and the JPL team accomplish in the years to come.” During the Artemis II test flight, Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen journeyed 695,081 miles on a lunar flyby that took them farther than any humans have ever traveled before. “It feels fitting for Reid, who with the Artemis II crew traveled farther from Earth than any human in history, to join Caltech and JPL — institutions that for nearly 90 years have sent spacecraft into the far reaches of our solar system and beyond,” said Dave Gallagher, JPL director and Caltech vice president. “Reid shares our drive for discovery, knows what it takes to lead teams through high-stakes missions, and has a remarkable ability to inspire people everywhere. He adds incredible bench strength to our leadership team as we build on the lab’s legacy and shape its future together.” After joining NASA’s astronaut corps in 2009, Wiseman went on to serve as flight engineer aboard the International Space Station for the 165-day Expedition 41 mission in 2014 and was a commander of NASA’s 21st Extreme Environment Mission Operations expedition, during which he lived for eight days in a habitat on the ocean floor in 2016. As the agency’s chief astronaut from December 2020 to November 2022, Wiseman led NASA’s astronaut corps, overseeing crew flight readiness and crew safety for all NASA human spaceflight missions. During his years of service at the agency, he has conducted hundreds of scientific experiments. “I’ve explored the furthest reaches of what a human can explore at NASA — and there were truly no words in the English vocabulary to describe seeing the Sun disappear behind the Moon from deep space. But that experience was really the jumping off point to go do the impossible things that Caltech and JPL dream, dare together, and do for NASA and the nation,” Wiseman said. “What an awesome time in my career to join this team and to try and push humanity and push our understanding of the solar system and the universe.” Wiseman joins JPL, NASA’s only federally funded research and development center, as the lab approaches its 90th anniversary since being founded by Caltech. In his role as Caltech’s associate vice president and JPL deputy director, Wiseman will be responsible for the strategic leadership, stewardship and continuous improvement of laboratory operations, including close partnership with Caltech on institutional planning, management and compliance. Serving as Center Management Authority for JPL mission execution, Wiseman will ensure operational excellence across mission support functions in accordance with NASA requirements and applicable federal and state regulations. In addition, he will be JPL’s primary interface for national security programs. “Reid brings to Caltech and JPL a truly unprecedented view of what humanity can achieve when ingenuity and determination are matched with the courage to pursue the furthest frontiers,” said Caltech president Ray Jayawardhana. “His pioneering spirit coupled with unbounded curiosity make him a natural fit for Caltech and JPL, a force-multiplier for a community whose daring continues to push the limits of humanity’s reach. I look forward to working closely with Dave and Reid as we chart our next era of exploration in partnership with NASA, elevating America’s space ambitions to breathtaking new heights.” After receiving a bachelor’s degree in computer and systems engineering from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, Wiseman joined the Navy, going on to fly combat missions and serve as a test pilot. He also has a master’s degree in systems engineering from Johns Hopkins University in his hometown of Baltimore. -end- Media Contact Matthew Segal Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Pasadena, Calif. 818-354-8307 matthew. J. Segal@jpl. Nasa. title: Cyclone Arnab hits Andhra coast as very severe cyclonic storm
content:
The first named storm of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season, Cyclone Arnab (pronounced “Or‑nab”), formed in the Bay of Bengal on 25 October, a later start than the basin’s usual April‑May naming period. A nighttime image captured by the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) on NOAA‑20 at 20:12 UTC on 26 October (1:42 a.m. India Standard Time on 27 October) showed the system with sustained winds of about 140 km h⁻¹, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD).

Arnab made landfall on the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coast early on 28 October, with sustained winds of 130 km h⁻¹. The IMD classifies a storm of this strength as a “very severe cyclonic storm,” which corresponds to a Category 1 storm on the Saffir‑Simpson hurricane wind scale. The landfall occurred between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, an area that includes large cities, agricultural land and fishing communities.

According to news reports, the cyclone caused extensive damage: trees were uprooted, crops and homes were inundated, fishing operations were limited, and transportation and power networks were disrupted. Prior to landfall, Indian authorities evacuated tens of thousands of people from vulnerable coastal zones.

Arnab arrived while an El Niño event was present—a climate pattern marked by warmer‑than‑normal equatorial Pacific waters that can modify global weather patterns. Research cited in the article notes that during El Niño years the Bay of Bengal typically experiences fewer and less intense tropical cyclones, a trend observed by scientists studying past cyclone activity.

The accompanying image was created by Michala Garrison using VIIRS day‑night band data from NASA’s EOSDIS LANCE, GIBS/Worldview and the Joint Polar Satellite System (JPSS). The story was written by Adam Voiland and references reports from the Associated Press, The Hindu, The Indian Express and the IMD’s National Bulletin.
summary: Cyclone Arnab hits Andhra coast as very severe cyclonic storm.
author: NASA News

title: APOD October 29 2026: Venus’s ‘Horns’ Crescent Seen Near New Moon Alignment
content: APOD Science APOD APOD: 29 October 2026 – The… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. The Horns of Venus Explanation: That’s no moon. But you could be forgiven for thinking it was a crescent Moon in the sky. It is a lesser known fact that Venus also has phases. (What about other planets? ) The featured image shows Venus seen almost directly between the Sun and the Earth. This happens once every year and a half, and it is like the alignment that happens every month during a new Moon. But the new Moon is dark, while Venus’ backlit atmosphere refracts and scatters the sunlight, creating a glowing crescent arc that extends beyond 180 degrees: the tips of this arc are called the “horns”. The crescent can be seen with a small telescope or binoculars during twilight, but those with exceptionally acute eyesight may be able to see it with the unaided eye. Ancient Babylonian astronomers may have been the first to study Venus’ brightness changes, which are related to its phases. Many other cultures have similar astronomical records, including the oldest surviving Maya book. Tomorrow’s picture: What’s next? title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked archive of 41,000 DHS employee records
content: Bluesky informed WIRED that it has blocked links to a leaked archive covering 41,000 employees of ICE, Customs and Border Protection, and other Department of Homeland Security agencies. The platform said the block was applied because the archive contains individuals’ contact information that was shared without authorization.
summary: Bluesky told WIRED it blocked links to a leaked archive of information on 41,000 ICE, CBP and other DHS workers. The archive contains the workers’ contact information that was shared without their authorization.
author: Wired

title: Anduril says BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch
content:
Anduril and Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, beginning with a single model in 2027. Anduril says its BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch.  

The companies also set a long‑term goal of pushing the computer industry to create a fully domestic supply chain.  

The announcement is notable because no major U.S. computer company currently builds laptops in the United States—Apple, Dell, HP, and Microsoft do not. Some firms have briefly assembled computers in the U.S. to appease President Donald Trump, but no company currently builds laptops domestically.
summary: Anduril and Qualcomm announced a partnership to build laptops entirely in the United States, starting with a single model in 2027. The companies said the BlueChip laptop will meet Buy American standards at launch and aim to push a fully domestic supply chain.
author: The Verge

title: Microsoft reports $92.3 bn quarterly revenue after offering buyouts to 60,000 staff
content:
Microsoft reported quarterly revenue of $92.3 billion and a profit of $36.6 billion, surpassing Wall Street expectations.  

The company’s growth was largely driven by its Azure cloud‑computing division, which expanded 48 % in the September quarter.  

Just days after offering voluntary buyouts to some 60,000 employees, Microsoft’s stock value rose billions of dollars in the market.
summary: Microsoft reports $92.3 bn quarterly revenue after offering buyouts to 60,000 staff.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Alphabet shares tumble over 10% after profit miss and ad slowdown
content:
Alphabet Inc. reported a July‑to‑September net profit of $26.2 billion, a 25 % decline from the same period a year earlier, and a per‑share earnings of $2.12. The company’s revenue rose to $127.6 billion, but analysts surveyed by FactSet had expected higher profit figures.

After the earnings release, Alphabet shares fell more than 10 % in after‑hours trading on Wednesday, erasing tens of billions of dollars in market value from the $4 trillion‑valued tech giant.

Investors cited the profit miss, a slowdown in the company’s advertising business, and continued large spending on artificial‑intelligence initiatives as reasons for the sharp drop in share price.
summary: Alphabet shares tumble over 10% after profit miss and ad slowdown.
author: Guardian Technology

title: 68 dead as two high‑speed trains collide south of Madrid, Spain's second fatal crash
content: At least 68 people died when two high-speed trains collided south of Madrid, Spain's second deadly rail crash this year. In Montreal, EU leaders meet Mark Carney to launch an 'Alliance for the Future'. We also look at next week's US midterms, Ukraine's defence capabilities, and rising oil prices.
summary: 68 dead as two high‑speed trains collide south of Madrid, Spain's second fatal crash.
author: Euronews

title: King Charles III dances at Junkanoo parade in Nassau during Caribbean tour
content: King Charles III was seen dancing during a vibrant Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas, on Wednesday, 28 October. The event was part of his first Caribbean tour since ascending the throne.
summary: King Charles III showed his dance moves during a colourful Junkanoo street parade in Nassau, the capital of the Bahamas. The event took place on Wednesday 28 October and was part of his first Caribbean tour since becoming monarch.
author: Euronews

title: Israel election may limit Netanyahu but retain war powers against Iran
content: Following Tuesday’s election, Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to serve as Israel’s caretaker prime minister and face greater constraints. Nonetheless, experts say his administration could still retain significant powers, including the authority to wage war against Iran. France 24’s International Affairs Editor Angela Diffley will provide further analysis of the election’s impact on Israel’s approach to Iran.
summary: Benjamin Netanyahu is expected to face greater constraints as Israel’s caretaker prime minister following Tuesday’s election. Experts say his government could retain significant powers, including the authority to wage war against Iran.
author: France 24

title: US grants visa to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro
content:
The U.S. State Department announced on Tuesday that it had granted entry visas to Brazilian senator Flavio Bolsonaro and his immediate family.  

Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami, Florida, on Wednesday after he declined to surrender his passports as ordered by Brazil’s Supreme Court in a money‑laundering investigation, as explained by France 24’s Kethevane Gorjestani.
summary: Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his immediate family landed in Miami, Florida on Wednesday after he refused to surrender passports ordered by the Supreme Court in a money‑laundering probe. The US State Department announced on Tuesday that it had granted entry visas to the senator and his family.
author: France 24

title: Dolores Huerta, US civil rights icon, dies at 96 in Bakersfield
content:
Influential US labour union co‑founder, feminist, and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday in Bakersfield, California, her family said.  

Credited with coining the enduring “Si, se puede!” rallying cry later adapted by former US president Barack Obama, Huerta continued her activism on race, poverty, LGBTQ, and women’s rights issues until the last months of her life.
summary: Dolores Huerta, US civil rights icon, dies at 96 in Bakersfield.
author: France 24

title: Putin courts African leaders at third Russia‑Africa Summit in Moscow
content: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with African leaders and government delegates on Wednesday in Moscow during the third Russia‑Africa Summit. The gathering focused on trade, security, arms deals and grain supplies, reflecting the Kremlin’s stated aim to broaden its presence across Africa.
summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin sought to woo African leaders and government delegates on Wednesday at the third Russia‑Africa Summit in Moscow. The summit covered trade, security, arms deals and grain supplies as part of the Kremlin's effort to expand its footprint in Africa.
author: France 24

title: Israeli election results show Netanyahu bloc at 53 seats, opposition leads with 67
content: With more than 90 % of ballots counted on Thursday, Israel’s election results show no party or bloc reaching a governing majority. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc holds 53 seats, while the opposition totals 67 seats, including 48 for Gadi Eisenkot’s centrist bloc and 19 for Arab‑majority parties. The Israeli president urged parties on Wednesday to “do everything” necessary to forge a coalition and prevent another round of elections. The liveblog continues to track developments as parties negotiate a possible government.
summary: Israeli election results show Netanyahu bloc at 53 seats, opposition leads with 67.
author: France 24

title: North Korea fires around a dozen short‑range ballistic missiles off east coast
content: North Korea launched roughly a dozen short‑range ballistic missiles from its east coast on Thursday, according to South Korea’s defence ministry. The missile launches follow a recent increase in weapons testing by Pyongyang, occurring despite Seoul’s offer to hold military talks.
summary: North Korea fired around a dozen short‑range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul's defence ministry said. Pyongyang has stepped up weapons tests in recent weeks despite South Korea's offer of military talks.
author: France 24

title: Liverpool beats Chelsea on penalties to reach League Cup quarter-finals
content: Liverpool advanced to the League Cup quarter‑finals after a 1‑1 draw with Chelsea was decided by a 6‑5 penalty shoot‑out win. Wesley Fofana missed his spot‑kick, sending it over the bar, which secured Chelsea’s elimination. Earlier in the match, French defender Maxence Lacroix left the field injured before half‑time, a week before the France squad is announced.
summary: Liverpool advanced to the League Cup quarter-finals by defeating Chelsea 6-5 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Chelsea's exit was sealed when Wesley Fofana missed his penalty, and defender Maxence Lacroix left the match injured before half-time.
author: France 24

title: Spain declares three days of mourning after high‑speed train crash kills 68
content: Spain entered three days of mourning on Thursday following a high‑speed train collision that killed 68 people and injured scores. The crash has sparked fresh questions about rail safety and management in the country.
summary: Spain entered three days of mourning on Thursday after a high‑speed train collision killed 68 people. The crash also injured scores and has prompted fresh questions about rail safety and management.
author: France 24

title: US voters elect new Congress in midterms, shaping future and Trump's second term
content: US voters are casting ballots to elect a new Congress. According to the source, the election outcome will be decisive for the United States’ future and will serve as a judgment on Donald Trump’s second term as president.
summary: US voters are electing a new Congress. The results will be decisive for the future of the United States and a judgment on Donald Trump's second term as president.
author: DW World

title: UN General Assembly backs end to Cuba embargo with weakest support in 20 years
content: The United Nations General Assembly voted on Wednesday to call for an end to the United States’ economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba for the 34th time. The resolution received the lowest level of support in twenty years.
summary: The United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time an end to the United States' economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba. The resolution received the weakest backing in two decades.
author: UN News

title: UN rights chief Volker Türk urges stronger civilian protection as youth protest
content: At a press briefing on Wednesday, UN human rights chief Volker Türk urged stronger protection of civilians in conflicts. He said youth‑led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing worldwide demand for reinforced human rights.
summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a Wednesday press briefing that youth‑led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for stronger human‑rights protection. He urged better protection of civilians in conflicts.
author: UN News

title: New York raises park to hold back sea after Hurricane Sandy
content: New York is undertaking a project to raise a park as a barrier against the sea, a response to the damage caused by Hurricane Sandy on 29 October 2012, when the storm surge flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.
summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires. New York is raising a park to hold back the sea.
author: UN News

title: Shell reports adjusted profit of $10.8bn, double prior quarter amid Middle East conflict
content:
Shell reported an adjusted profit of $10.8 bn (£8.1 bn) for the July‑September quarter, more than double the $5.432 bn earned in the previous quarter. The jump was attributed to higher oil and gas prices and global shortages driven by the Middle East conflict.  

The figure surpassed analysts’ forecast of $10.33 bn. In addition, Shell announced a $5 bn return to shareholders, a move that comes amid criticism from climate campaigners over the company’s high profits.
summary: Shell reports adjusted profit of $10.8bn, double prior quarter amid Middle East conflict.
author: Guardian World

title: Defence department secretary backs claim that sharing Senate hearing footage could invite bullying
content:
A senior defence official sought a Senate hearing to bar the release of footage showing public servants giving evidence on social media, arguing it could invite online bullying and raise national‑security concerns. The secretary of the defence department, Meghan Quinn, approved the idea.

Freedom‑of‑information emails obtained by Guardian Australia show that deputy secretary Celia Perkins had planned the request to the parliamentary inquiry. The proposal was flagged to the offices of deputy prime minister Richard Marles and assistant defence minister Peter Khalil before receiving Quinn’s backing.
summary: Defence department secretary backs claim that sharing Senate hearing footage could invite bullying.
author: Guardian World

title: 19-year-old Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau dies after masked gunmen shoot crowd outside Brisbane pub
content:
A 19‑year‑old woman, Vana‑Reese Schuster‑Togiatau of Jimboomba, died after a drive‑by shooting outside Fitzy’s Loganholme pub in Brisbane’s south on Saturday night.  

Masked gunmen opened fire into a crowd outside the venue, striking Schuster‑Togiatau in the head and neck. The attack left three other people injured. The incident is being treated as a serious crime by police.
summary: Vana-Reese Schuster-Togiatau, a 19-year-old from Jimboomba, was hit in the head and neck when masked gunmen opened fire into a crowd outside Fitzy’s Loganholme in Brisbane’s south on Saturday night. The drive-by shooting also injured three other people.
author: Guardian World

title: Coroner urges TGA to review unapproved peptides after actor Richard Norton's death
content: A coroner has urged Australia’s Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) to review the regulation of unapproved peptide drugs following the death of Richard Norton, a 75‑year‑old film‑industry fight choreographer, stuntman and martial artist. Norton suffered cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting a prescribed but unapproved combination of the peptides CJC1295 and ipamorelin. The coroner’s call reflects concerns that the incident could lead to stricter controls on such substances.
summary: Richard Norton, a 75‑year‑old Australian film industry fight choreographer, stuntman and martial artist, went into cardiac arrest in March 2025 after injecting the prescribed but unapproved peptides CJC1295 and ipamorelin. A coroner has called on the Therapeutic Goods Administration to review the use of such unapproved peptides.
author: Guardian World

title: South Korean families urge removal of Seoul crush footage from Call of Duty 4
content:
Bereaved families in South Korea have asked the publisher of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to remove a clip from the game that depicts a figure performing CPR while bodies lie on a street.  

The seconds‑long footage, which the families say comes from the deadly 2022 Seoul crowd crush, appears in the opening moments of the game and is used to portray civilian casualties during a fictional North Korean invasion.
summary: South Korean families urge removal of Seoul crush footage from Call of Duty 4.
author: Guardian World

title: Amnesty alleges Cambodian police, soldiers guarded abusive scam compounds
content:
Amnesty International’s report says survivors of Cambodian scam compounds allege that serving police and military officers acted as private security guards at sites where thousands were forced to work in the online‑fraud industry. The survivors claim the officers administered electric shocks and beatings, and that some guards used electric batons to keep people trapped.

The rights group asserts that the officers were employed by security companies that formed part of a system enabling slavery and rape within the compounds. Amnesty’s findings focus on the alleged role of these serving officers in the abuse and coercion reported by the victims.
summary: Survivors told Amnesty International that serving Cambodian police and military officers acted as private security guards in scam compounds where thousands were forced to work in online fraud. The group said the guards administered electric shocks, beatings and used electric batons, contributing to slavery and rape in the compounds.
author: Guardian World

title: Sanrio ends partnership with Japanese drama Vivant after Chinese outcry
content: Sanrio ends association with TV drama Vivant after China says portrayal of ruthless Chinese agents is ‘deliberate smear’ The company behind the successful Hello Kitty franchise has apologised and ended its commercial tie-up with a Japanese TV drama after Chinese state media and netizens condemned the show’s “deliberate smears” against China. Sanrio, a Japanese firm whose characters are popular around the world, said in a post on the Chinese social media site Weibo that it had decided to end its association with the TV drama Vivant after concluding that it “contained elements inconsistent with Sanrio’s core values”.
summary: Sanrio, the maker of Hello Kitty, apologized and ended its commercial tie‑up with the Japanese TV drama Vivant. The move came after Chinese state media and netizens condemned the show as a deliberate smear of Chinese agents, and Sanrio said in a Weibo post that the drama contained elements inconsistent with its core values.
author: Guardian World

title: Gerónimo Rulli saves decisive penalty as Manchester City beats Brighton 4-3 in shootout
content: Jérémy Doku’s second‑half substitute appearance turned Manchester City into a high‑octane proposition, sparking momentum that carried into the penalty shootout. Enzo Maresca’s men ultimately triumphed 4‑3, with Gerónimo Rulli the hero. Rulli’s decisive save from Lewis Dunk’s fifth spot‑kick and his earlier clearance of Yasin Ayari’s fourth effort sealed the victory.
summary: Jérémy Doku entered as a second‑half substitute and helped Manchester City build momentum into a penalty shootout. Manchester City won 4‑3 after Gerónimo Rulli saved Lewis Dunk’s fifth spot‑kick and Yasin Ayari’s fourth.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Stan Wawrinka Retires After Basel Loss to Jiri Lehecka
content: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka announced his retirement in front of a home crowd in Basel. The decision followed his straight-sets defeat by Jiri Lehecka in the opening round of the Swiss Indoors.
summary: Three-time Grand Slam champion Stan Wawrinka retired in front of his home crowd in Basel. He lost in straight sets to Jiri Lehecka in the opening round of the Swiss Indoors.
author: BBC Sport

title: Maresca: Rulli heroics cause no worries for Donnarumma
content: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has expressed confidence in Gianluigi Donnarumma's status as the team's primary goalkeeper, despite Geronimo Rulli's recent penalty shootout performances. Maresca stated that there are no concerns regarding Donnarumma's position, affirming that Rulli understands his specific role within the squad.
summary: Geronimo Rulli's penalty shootout performances have created pressure for Gianluigi Donnarumma at Manchester City. Manager Enzo Maresca stated he has no doubt about Donnarumma's status as the number one goalkeeper.
author: BBC Sport

title: Unbeaten Chelsea return to best form after 2-0 Women's Champions League win over Roma
content: Chelsea have returned to peak form after securing a 2-0 victory over Roma in the Women's Champions League. The club is currently enjoying an unbeaten run, having built their recent success on this strong performance.
summary: Chelsea secured a 2-0 victory over Roma in the Women's Champions League. The team is currently on an unbeaten run and is described as getting back to their best form.
author: BBC Sport

title: Stevens fiance backs Rogers over El-Sayed in Michigan Senate race
content: Jason Turkish, the fiancé of Representative Haley Stevens, stated this week that he will support Republican candidate Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan’s Senate race. In a Wednesday interview, Turkish accused El-Sayed, Stevens’s former Democratic primary rival, of using antisemitic language on the campaign trail.
summary: Jason Turkish, the fiance of Rep. Haley Stevens, stated he will support GOP candidate Mike Rogers over Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan's Senate race. Turkish accused El-Sayed of using antisemitic language on the campaign trail during an interview published Wednesday.
author: The Hill

title: Murkowski demands truth from Peltola amid alleged ballot-stacking
content: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) called for the “truth” from former Rep. Mary Peltola (D-Alaska) amid what she said was a “pattern of lies and coverups” following reports the Democrat’s campaign recruited one of her midterm opponents to “ballot-stack.” “While some may try to write this off as just how politics works now, ballot-stacking should have…
summary: Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) called for the “truth” from former Rep.
author: The Hill

title: DOJ asks judge to keep Ilhan Omar search warrant sealed
content: Federal prosecutors requested on Tuesday that a judge deny a motion by over a dozen news organizations to unseal the search warrant for Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minn.) Washington, D.C., home. The Justice Department argued that immediate disclosure could jeopardize the ongoing criminal investigation. The motion was detailed in a heavily redacted filing signed by Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia.
summary: Federal prosecutors requested a judge to reject a news organizations' bid to unseal the search warrant for Rep. Ilhan Omar's home. They argued that unsealing the document could jeopardize the ongoing criminal investigation.
author: The Hill

title: Kilmeade, Hume say Vance ‘not as popular as he thinks he is’ ahead of 2028
content: Fox News hosts Brian Kilmeade and Brit Hume expressed skepticism on Wednesday regarding Vice President Vance’s 2028 presidential prospects. They questioned whether his close association with President Trump might negatively impact his chances of securing the Republican nomination. Kilmeade stated that he does not believe Vance is as popular among Republicans as the Vice President assumes.
summary: Kilmeade, Hume say Vance ‘not as popular as he thinks he is’ ahead of 2028.
author: The Hill

title: LJI and UW scientists find mutated immune cells in lupus patients
content: Researchers at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology and the University of Washington have identified unusual mutations in the immune cells of patients with lupus. The study suggests these mutations may transform the bodies of affected individuals into battlegrounds.
summary: Researchers at the La Jolla Institute for Immunology and the University of Washington discovered unusual mutations in patients with lupus. These mutations may turn the bodies of these patients into battlegrounds.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: LA fire smoke exposed millions to lead levels 80x above background
content: A new study indicates that millions of Los Angeles residents were exposed to toxic lead levels from smoke 80 times higher than typical background levels during a 24-hour period at the height of the 2025 fires.
summary: A new study found that millions of Los Angeles residents were exposed to toxic lead levels in smoke during the 2025 fires. The exposure occurred over a 24-hour period and was 80 times higher than the typical background level.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Wider surgical margins may not improve cancer control
content: Surgeons frequently face the dilemma of determining how much surrounding healthy tissue to remove to ensure complete cancer elimination. Removing larger margins can result in the loss of nearby nerves, blood vessels, tendons, and joints, leading to lasting negative effects on a patient's quality of life.
summary: Surgeons often face the challenge of determining how much healthy tissue to remove to ensure cancer is fully eliminated. Removing more tissue can damage nearby nerves, blood vessels, tendons, and joints, which negatively impacts a patient's quality of life.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Achilles injections show no benefit over sham treatment
content: A clinical trial published in The BMJ reports that injections commonly used to treat Achilles tendinopathy provide no meaningful clinical benefit over sham treatment. The condition, characterized by pain, stiffness, and swelling in the Achilles tendon, was the focus of this study, which found no significant advantage for the active injections compared to placebo.
summary: A clinical trial published by The BMJ found that injections for Achilles tendinopathy offer no meaningful clinical advantage over placebo. The study addresses pain, stiffness, and swelling in the Achilles tendon.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Video decision aid increases advance care planning in seniors with chronic kidney disease
content: A study published in JAMA Internal Medicine found that a video decision aid increases advance care planning documentation in the electronic health records of older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease. The research was released to coincide with Kidney Week, the annual meeting of the American Society of Nephrology, held from October 21 to 25 in Denver.
summary: Among older adults with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD), a video decision aid increases advance care planning (ACP) documentation in the electronic health record, according to a study published in JAMA Internal Medicine to coincide with Kidney Week, the annual meeting of the American Society of Nephrology, held from Oct. 21 to 25 in Denver.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Targeting gibberellin action reveals how plant hormone coordinates root growth
content: Conventional hormone treatments typically activate signaling throughout an entire plant, making it difficult to determine the specific cells and tissues where plant hormones must act to influence growth and development.
summary: Plant hormones influence growth and development by acting on specific cells and tissues. Determining precisely where and when a hormone needs to act has been challenging because conventional treatment activates signaling throughout the plant.
author: Phys.org

title: Molecular architecture determines tomato plant resistance to its main pest
content:
An international study has identified the spatial structure of a plant defense molecule as the key factor making wild tomatoes more resistant to the tomato leafminer (Phthorimaea absoluta) than cultivated varieties. The researchers mapped the biochemical origin of this difference, demonstrating that altering four amino acids in a single enzyme is sufficient to change the substance’s structure and increase its toxicity against the pest.

This discovery highlights the role of molecular architecture in plant defense mechanisms. The findings pave the way for developing resistant tomato varieties through gene editing, offering a potential solution to the damage caused by this main pest.
summary: Molecular architecture determines tomato plant resistance to its main pest.
author: Phys.org

title: Atomic magnetism shows iron, not chromium, drives sunlight‑produced ammonia
content: Research teams at the University of Vienna and TU Wien investigated sunlight‑driven ammonia‑producing catalysts. Two nearly identical materials behaved differently. In the active catalysts, tiny triangles of three iron atoms are essential; replacing those iron atoms with chromium stops the reaction entirely.
summary: Research teams at the University of Vienna and TU Wien studied catalysts that use sunlight to produce ammonia. When the three iron atoms that form tiny triangles in these catalysts are replaced by chromium atoms, the chemical reaction no longer takes place.
author: Phys.org

title: IrMn ultrathin layer enhances spin signals in magnetic insulator–platinum structure
content: Researchers at Kyushu University discovered that an ultrathin layer of iridium manganese (IrMn) can enhance two spin‑related signals in a structure composed of a magnetic insulator and a platinum film. By studying how spin currents are generated and absorbed, the team gained insight into how the intermediate IrMn layer improves spin transfer. The results could inform the development of ultralow‑power devices for computing and energy harvesting.
summary: Researchers at Kyushu University have found that an ultrathin layer of iridium manganese (IrMn) can improve two spin-related signals in a structure made of a magnetic insulator and a platinum film. By examining how spin currents are generated and absorbed, the team gained insights into how the intermediate layer improves spin transfer.
author: Phys.org

title: Phantom Lighthouse Illusion Persists at Lady Elliot Island, Australia
content:
Two lighthouses stand on Lady Elliot Island, the southernmost point of Australia’s Great Barrier Reef. The original beacon was erected in 1873 and remained in service until 1995, when a newer structure assumed the role of warning ships off the reef. The island’s second lighthouse has since become the primary navigational aid for maritime traffic in the area.  

Visitors to the island frequently report sightings of a third, nonexistent lighthouse. At night, they describe beams of light appearing far off on the horizon, as if a phantom lighthouse were operating. These reports have led some to speculate about an unseen beacon, though no physical structure or operational light is present.
summary: Lady Elliot Island hosts two lighthouses, one built in 1873 and the other taking over in 1995. Visitors frequently report seeing a third, nonexistent lighthouse beam at night, creating a phantom illumination on the horizon.
author: Phys.org

title: Study examines Indian Ocean's impact on Europe's early‑winter rain and storms
content: Scientists are investigating how the Indian Ocean may influence Europe’s early‑winter weather. Though Atlantic storms, cold northern air, and Mediterranean rain are the usual suspects, researchers are exploring whether an ocean thousands of kilometres away can leave a detectable signature on Europe’s early winter. In their study, the authors ask whether the Indian Ocean’s conditions can be linked to the patterns of rain and storms that affect Europe during the early winter months.
summary: Researchers investigated whether the Indian Ocean can leave a detectable signature on Europe's early‑winter rain and storms. Their work explores how distant oceanic conditions may influence familiar European weather systems.
author: Phys.org

title: Ecologist Steven Allison highlights microbes' role in climate fight in new book
content: Ecologist Steven Allison argues that microbes play a vital role in combating climate change, a point he makes in his book The Age of Microbes. Christa Lesté‑Lasserre notes the book’s convincing and hopeful tone.
summary: Ecologist Steven Allison argues that microbes are important for fighting climate change. He makes this case in his book The Age of Microbes, according to Christa Lesté-Lasserre.
author: New Scientist

title: Hacker 'Department of Peace' steals over 41,000 DHS employee records via Okta
content:
A hacker stole a trove of personal information from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The breach exposes the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations of more than 41,000 employees, including those in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), according to TechCrunch and Wired.

The data also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools. As reported by TechCrunch, a hacker known as “Department of Peace” gained access to the data through Okta, an identity and access management service used by the DHS. Around 21,000 records pertain to CBP employees.
summary: A hacker known as "Department of Peace" accessed DHS data through Okta and stole personal information of more than 41,000 employees, including those at ICE and CBP. The breach revealed names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, office locations, and linked agencies to specific surveillance tools.
author: The Verge

title: Instagram head Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI will worsen
content:
Instagram head Adam Mosseri stated that negative sentiment toward artificial intelligence is expected to intensify. In an interview on the Colin and Samir podcast, where he discussed the platform’s new widescreen and long-form video features, Mosseri acknowledged that many people dislike AI, a sentiment not limited to young people or creatives. He described a growing trend of anxiety, frustration, and anger regarding the technology, particularly within creative industries.

Mosseri predicted that these emotions will continue to escalate, noting that the situation is not only worsening but will keep getting worse. He anticipates seeing further frustration and anger, acknowledging that some of these reactions are founded while others are not.
summary: Instagram head Adam Mosseri said that many people dislike AI, especially in creative industries, and that negativity will continue to worsen. He discussed this on the Colin and Samir podcast while announcing Instagram's new widescreen and long‑form video features.
author: The Verge

title: Apple unveils touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
content:
Apple unveiled its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years, announcing a laptop that combines an OLED screen with a touchscreen—an option that macOS has offered for the first time. The company noted that the move follows long‑standing internal debate, recalling former CEO Steve Jobs’ opposition to touch input.

In a demonstration video, users interacted with the device by reaching up to touch the display, performing file‑dragging and multi‑touch gestures such as pinch‑to‑zoom. The footage showed the laptop in a conventional, non‑convertible configuration, indicating that the design is not a 2‑in‑1 convertible.

Apple calls the OLED panel the PROLED XDR. It can reach 2,000 nits of maximum brightness and offers a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. Burn‑in protection was mentioned, though the specific approach has not yet been disclosed. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of previous models.
summary: Apple announced its first major MacBook Pro redesign in over five years, adding a touchscreen and an OLED display called PROLED XDR. The OLED screen can reach 2,000 nits brightness, 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and retains a 120 Hz variable refresh rate, while burn‑in protection was mentioned but not detailed.
author: Ars Technica

title: Kennedy Unilaterally Grants Specialty Pharmacies Access to Six Peptide Drugs
content: Anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy has unilaterally passed a rule that will allow specialty pharmacies to sell six specific peptide drugs, overruling scientists at the Food and Drug Administration. The peptides are popular among members of Kennedy's Make America Health Again movement and many prominent MAHA figures and Kennedy allies sell them. Kennedy said he uses some of the peptides and called himself a "big fan." But FDA scientists continue to say there is insufficient evidence to show if they're effective and they are potentially dangerous. In 2023, the safety concerns led the FDA to remove the six peptides from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies called compounding pharmacies—which make customized formulations of drugs for patients, or, in cases such as this, specialty drugs in bulk. Kennedy's new rule sidesteps the need to formally undo that FDA action. The rule is titled "Enforcement Discretion Policy Regarding 503A Compounding Using Certain Peptide Bulk Drug Substances" and was made available Wednesday on the Federal Register, with the final publication data set for October 30. The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action against compounding pharmacies for making the peptides, essentially giving them a green light to freely produce and sell them. Kennedy had quietly proposed this rule earlier this month. Read full article Comments
summary: Kennedy Unilaterally Grants Specialty Pharmacies Access to Six Peptide Drugs.
author: Ars Technica

title: EU plans first subsea cable linking Europe to Greenland, bypassing US
content: The European Union plans to create the first subsea Internet cable directly connecting Europe to Greenland. The Pan-Arctic Cable project could also extend to Canada and eventually link with Japan and South Korea, notably bypassing the United States. The Pan-Arctic Cable is described as a European Union flagship project in a European Commission joint communication published on October 20, 2026. The policy document describes a new European strategy for the Arctic that supports “a sovereign, secure and resilient submarine cable connection linking Greenland directly to the EU,” while also suggesting that “like-minded partners like Canada” could provide a stepping stone for future cable expansion toward Asia. “It is interesting that this project is even being considered, because five years ago it would have seemed like not a particularly commercially attractive proposition,” Elisabeth Braw, a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative, told Ars. “But the fact that it's being considered is very much on trend and a sign of our times.” Read full article Comments
summary: The European Union plans the Pan‑Arctic Cable, the first subsea Internet cable to directly connect Europe to Greenland. The project could later extend to Canada and Asia, bypassing the United States.
author: Ars Technica

title: ULA to launch Vulcan rocket on Nov. 13 to deploy Amazon Leo satellites
content:
United Launch Alliance (ULA) announced on Wednesday that its Vulcan rocket is slated to return to flight on November 13, nine months after a solid‑rocket‑booster anomaly disrupted the company’s 2026 launch schedule. The scheduled mission will carry 40 satellites for Amazon’s Leo broadband constellation, marking the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon has booked to deploy the bulk of its network.

The launch will lift off from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, though ULA said the date remains pending range approval. The flight is critical for ULA, which has faced nozzle failures on its solid‑rocket boosters during two of its first four missions, most recently in February. Although the rocket completed those missions despite the failures, officials at the U.S. Space Force, ULA’s primary customer, reportedly lost confidence in the Vulcan program.
summary: United Launch Alliance announced it will return its Vulcan rocket to flight on November 13, launching 40 satellites for Amazon's Leo broadband constellation from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station. The launch follows a nine‑month pause caused by solid rocket booster nozzle failures that eroded confidence from the US Space Force, ULA's primary customer.
author: Ars Technica

title: Microsoft Reveals Azure Revenue of $33.2 Billion
content: Microsoft has announced Azure’s revenue for the first time in dollar terms, reporting $33.2 billion. The company previously had not disclosed Azure’s quarterly earnings in dollars. The disclosure highlights how close Azure is approaching the market leader, Amazon Web Services.
summary: Microsoft has disclosed Azure's quarterly revenue in dollars for the first time. The revenue of $33.2 billion shows Azure is close to surpassing AWS.
author: TechCrunch

title: Israeli electorate shifts rightward, deepening societal fracture, RAND scholar says
content:
Erin Ogunkeye welcomed Dr. Shira Efron, RAND’s Distinguished Israel Policy Chair, who said many, including herself, “underestimated the extent of the fracture in Israeli society.” She linked the fracture to a political system marked by ideological polarization, a rightward shift of the Jewish electorate and contested legitimacy of Arab political participation, which she said has sharply narrowed coalition‑building options.  

Dr. Efron described a landscape where Prime Minister Netanyahu’s governing bloc has lost ground but still possesses “more cards, or better cards, to play,” including the possibility of another election, a national‑unity government or efforts to draw opposition partners into its orbit.
summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Dr. Shira Efron, RAND's Distinguished Israel Policy Chair.
author: France 24

title: Spain high‑speed train collision south of Madrid kills 68, injures over 100
content:
A high‑speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, authorities said, with the death toll expected to rise. The incident is described as one of Europe’s deadliest high‑speed rail disasters of the century.

It is the second such accident in Spain this year, prompting renewed scrutiny of rail safety. The transport minister referred to an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” as causes of the crash. France 24’s Sarah Morris reported from Urda, south of Madrid.
summary: A high‑speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday. Authorities said the toll may rise and the transport minister cited an “error” and “inexplicable circumstances” in Spain’s second such accident this year.
author: France 24

title: EU natural gas prices exceed €100/MWh, highest since 2022
content:
European natural‑gas prices have risen above €100 per megawatt hour, the highest level recorded since 2022, as winter approaches. The EU says it is not worried about supplies, noting that storage facilities are 72 % full, but it warns households that a “difficult” season lies ahead.

In related coverage, the UK government is taking steps to cushion the impact of high energy bills, while 200 passengers have been left stranded in Cambodia after a multi‑year cruise was cancelled because of high fuel costs.
summary: European natural gas price rose above €100 per megawatt hour, its highest level since 2022. The EU said it is not worried about supplies despite storage at 72% capacity and warned households of a difficult winter season.
author: France 24

title: Spain launches investigation after second fatal high‑speed train crash kills 68
content: Spain’s rail safety is under scrutiny as officials open an investigation into Wednesday’s high‑speed train collision. The crash, the nation’s second fatal rail incident this year, killed at least 68 people and injured roughly 100 others. Authorities are probing the cause of the accident.
summary: Authorities have opened an official investigation into Wednesday's high‑speed train collision that killed at least 68 people and wounded around 100. The crash is Spain's second fatal rail incident this year, prompting questions about rail safety.
author: France 24

title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he is Brazil’s rightful leader after fleeing to US
content: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro's defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Fabio de Sa e Silva, Associate Professor of International Studies at the University of Oklahoma. He says that an attempt by Bolsonaro to turn a domestic dispute into a wider international issue "will not be successful", explaining that he is likely going to be "losing the grip of the opposition, there is a vacuum now that others will seek to occupy" and that it's unlikely that the United States will "get involved into questioning the results of the Brazilian election".
summary: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro's defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday.
author: France 24

title: Spain rail crash that killed 68 caused by erroneous train order, minister says
content: A rail collision in Spain’s central Castilla‑La Mancha region killed at least 68 people on Wednesday. According to the transport minister, the disaster occurred after a train was ordered to proceed in “error” despite a technical failure that had halted all services. The minister’s comments come as the first findings of the accident emerge, prompting renewed scrutiny of rail safety in the country. The incident follows a high‑speed collision in January that resulted in 46 deaths. France 24’s James Vasina reported the statements.
summary: A rail collision in Spain’s central Castilla‑La Mancha region killed at least 68 people on Wednesday. The transport minister said the crash happened after a train was ordered to go in error despite a technical failure that halted all services, and the findings may revive safety questions after a January high‑speed collision that killed 46.
author: France 24

title: Canada and EU abandon associate membership plan to deepen ties
content: Canada and the European Union have abandoned a proposal for associate EU membership, according to a joint declaration issued ahead of Thursday’s summit in Montreal. The two sides will pursue closer ties, while Prime Minister Mark Carney seeks to reduce Canada’s reliance on the United States, despite warnings from Donald Trump.
summary: Canada and the European Union will pursue closer ties and have dropped a proposal for associate EU membership, according to a joint declaration ahead of Thursday’s summit in Montreal. Prime Minister Mark Carney is seeking to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US, despite warnings from Donald Trump.
author: France 24

title: Budget 2026 adds £100 energy payment, raises bank tax as OBR forecasts 1% living‑standard rise
content:
The Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) has projected that living standards will rise by only 1 % over the entire post‑Covid decade.  

During a briefing, Martin Lewis reported that Chancellor John Healey confirmed the removal of standing charges from gas bills and expressed a desire to eliminate those charges from electricity bills as well. Lewis added that the chancellor will consult with Ofgem on how to achieve this, noting that the process is “trickier” and will take longer.
summary: Budget 2026 adds £100 energy payment, raises bank tax as OBR forecasts 1% living‑standard rise.
author: Guardian World

title: Nigel Farage skips budget over fear of seating‑arrangement altercation
content:
Nigel Farage, the leader of Reform UK, did not attend the chancellor’s first Budget 2026 in the House of Commons. He said he had left the chamber because he feared a “physical altercation” with another MP over seating arrangements.  

After the session, Farage held a press conference in which he expressed that he was “shocked” by the £10 bn pledged to support Ukraine. He also reiterated his party’s position on cutting tax for crypto investors.
summary: Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, missed the chancellor’s first budget because he feared a physical altercation with another MP over seating arrangements. After the budget he held a press conference saying he was shocked by the £10bn pledged to Ukraine and reiterated his party’s call to cut tax for crypto investors.
author: Guardian World

title: Anthony Williams on trial for attempted murder of 10 on LNER train
content: A court heard that a knifeman “caused terror and fear on an unimaginable scale” after stabbing 10 people on a London‑bound LNER train. The accused, 33‑year‑old Anthony Williams, is charged with attempting to murder ten passengers and staff on the train on 1 November of last year. Prosecutors also allege that Williams stabbed four additional people in the 24 hours preceding the train attack.
summary: Anthony Williams, 33, is accused of attempting to murder 10 passengers and staff on an LNER train on 1 November. He also allegedly stabbed four people in the 24 hours before the attack.
author: Guardian World

title: Healey raises taxes on banks, landlords to fund £100 handout for 20 million households
content: Few surprises as chancellor uses low-key speech blaming ‘global economic storms’ for stoking energy prices and cost of living crisis Budget 2026: key points at a glance Briefing: key questions answered by Heather Stewart and Pippa Crerar Editorial: Budget’s bold ambitions and welcome first steps John Healey raised taxes on banks and landlords to fund a £100 winter handout for 20 million families as official forecasts made clear there is no end in sight for the cost of living crisis. In his first budget, the chancellor blamed “global economic storms” for the grim outlook, as the war in Iran drives up oil and gas prices.
summary: John Healey increased taxes on banks and landlords to finance a £100 winter handout for 20 million families. He blamed “global economic storms” and the war in Iran for rising oil and gas prices.
author: Guardian World

title: Russell Brand admits misusing fame to facilitate sex during rape trial
content: Former comedian, in court on rape and sexual assault charges, says he misused position but ‘consent is more important than sex itself’ Russell Brand has told a court that he was wrong to have used his fame and success to “facilitate” sexual activity with women. The 51-year-old comedian said he had “misused” his position “very selfishly” and dedicated his life to “reckless philandering and idiocy”.
summary: Russell Brand, a 51‑year‑old former comedian, is in court on rape and sexual assault charges. He told the court he misused his fame and success to facilitate sexual activity with women and said consent is more important than sex.
author: Guardian World

title: Jared Kushner threatens lawsuit over new book alleging Gulf‑funded slush accounts
content: Kushner threatens to sue, denying allegations that two slush funds were set up to influence his Middle East role A new book containing incendiary claims about Jared Kushner ’s financial dealings during Donald Trump ’s first term has ignited a political and media firestorm. The book by author Matthew Cole is called Princes and Thieves: Jared Kushner and Mohamed bin Zayed’s Secret Plot to Remake the Middle East and was released in the US this week. An excerpt was published by Vanity Fair last Thursday, and immediately drew a furious response from Kushner, who called its claims “completely insane”. The book contains numerous allegations about Kushner, whose father-in-law is Trump and who has served as one of his top diplomatic envoys in the Middle East – the most explosive of which are claims linking him to huge bank accounts allegedly funded by Gulf states.
summary: Jared Kushner threatens lawsuit over new book alleging Gulf‑funded slush accounts.
author: Guardian World

title: Albania fines demonstrators $6,000 for being present at violent protests
content:
Albania has introduced fines exceeding $6,000 for anyone present at a protest that turns violent, even if the individual does not personally engage in violent acts. The penalty, described as six times the average monthly salary, is aimed at curbing gatherings that call for the prime minister’s resignation.

The measure comes as the capital, Tirana, has experienced months of anti‑government demonstrations that have recently escalated into pitched battles between security forces and protesters.
summary: Albania introduced fines of more than $6,000, six times the average monthly salary, for demonstrators present at protests that turn violent even if they do not personally commit violent acts. The measure comes as anti‑government protests in Tirana calling for the prime minister’s resignation have escalated into pitched battles with security forces.
author: Guardian World

title: Australian SAS officers aware of illegal throwdowns on dead Afghans, report finds
content: Nothing done to stop planting weapons on dead Afghans, ADF inspector says, as ‘breakdown of command’ allowed ‘egregious behaviour’ Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast Some Australian SAS officers knew that soldiers under their command were using “throwdowns” – planting weapons on dead Afghan civilians to portray them as combatants – but did nothing to stop the unlawful practice, a previously unpublished military report has said. Posted online this week, the executive summary of a 2021 investigation into the “cultural context” of the special operations command by the inspector general of the Australian Defence Force (IGADF) is scathing about the “breakdown of command” and the erosion of military discipline during special forces operations in Afghanistan, which “resulted in episodes of potential and actual egregious behaviour”.
summary: Australian SAS officers aware of illegal throwdowns on dead Afghans, report finds.
author: Guardian World

title: Meet Apeiron, Virgin Galactic's 1st 'Delta-class' space plane
content: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-gen "Delta" line, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name. Spaceship Apeiron will be the first Delta-class vehicle, Virgin Galactic revealed on Wednesday (Oct. 28). Apeiron (pronounced "A'-per-on," according to the announcement) takes its name from the ancient Greek word meaning "boundless," and was selected through a public poll that drew votes from thousands of people across 83 countries and six continents. The reveal comes on the same day that the space plane is scheduled to be flown from its manufacturing facility in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where the vehicle will undergo final preparations before beginning flight tests. Apeiron was one of four finalist names that Virgin Galactic narrowed down from a list of 276 employee-submitted suggestions. After the public weighed in, Apeiron came out on top over Horizon, Explorer and Ascend. “Apeiron, the Boundless, captures the ambition of human spaceflight and the possibilities it opens for humanity," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Golglazier said in a company statement. "The extraordinary response to the public vote made choosing this name even more meaningful." The shiny new space plane will be attached to Virgin Galactic's VMS Eve carrier aircraft for its journey to Spaceport America, where engineers will complete work on its avionics software ahead of Apeiron's first flight tests and eventual operational missions. The new Delta-class vehicle replaces Virgin's earlier space plane model, VSS Unity, which flew seven suborbital missions during its operational lifetime between the summers of 2023 and 2024. The company suspended VSS Unity flights to focus efforts on Apeiron's development, and now hopes to begin flying customers again in mid-2027. Each Delta-class vehicle is equipped to accommodate up to six passengers. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Once they're in regular operation, Virgin plans to fly each of its Delta-class vehicles as many as eight times a month. A second Delta-class space plane is already under construction and is expected to join Apeiron at Spaceport America around the same time that Virgin restarts flying passengers, about 675 of whom are still waiting in line with tickets for a seat on one of the company's suborbital jaunts, according to the company's Q2 2026 SEC filing. Now, more than 100 of those future space travelers are beginning their initial preparations for flight, with more ticketholders expected to follow once Virgin brings the second Delta-class vehicle into service. When the company began selling seats aboard its space plane in 2014, when VSS Unity was still under construction, tickets were priced around $200,000. Today, that price has jumped to $850,000 per seat, according to a report by Latte. (Image credit: Virgin Galactic) Like its predecessor, Apeiron and future Delta-class vehicles are designed for short, suborbital spaceflights, and are not capable of reaching orbit around Earth. They fly above the internationally recognized boundary of space, the 100-kilometer-high (62 miles) Karman line, and provide those onboard with several minutes of weightlessness and great views of the planet below. Virgin Galactic plans to share further details about its upcoming flight tests during its November earnings call. Virgin is one of two American companies that have flown paying customers to suborbital space and back. The other, Blue Origin, suspended its flights earlier this year to focus on helping land NASA astronauts on the moon.
summary: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-gen "Delta" line, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name. Spaceship Apeiron will be the first Delta-class vehicle, Virgin Galactic revealed on Wednesday (Oct.
author: Space.com

title: ‘We sold out tickets within 13 minutes’: new novel from romantasy author Sarah J Maas sparks fan mania
content:
The release of Sarah J Maas’s new novel, A Court of Splendered Harmony, has generated significant excitement among fans across the UK. The book marks the first installment in her A Court of Thorns and Roses series in over five years, prompting various bookshops to host special events to celebrate the launch.

In Leamington Spa, the romance bookshop The Spicy Librarian organized a masquerade ball to mark the occasion. According to co-founder Ali Maynard James, 6,000 people attempted to purchase 220 available tickets, causing the shop’s website to crash as soon as sales began. The tickets sold out within 13 minutes.

To commemorate the event, The Spicy Librarian hired a stately home for the celebration. This shop was part of a broader trend of UK bookshops holding parties and staying open past midnight on Monday night to welcome readers for the highly anticipated release.
summary: ‘We sold out tickets within 13 minutes’: new novel from romantasy author Sarah J Maas sparks fan mania.
author: Guardian Culture

title: Inter returns to Serie A top after late own goals; Milan lose at home to Bologna
content:
Inter returned to the top of Serie A with a 2-0 victory over bottom-side Venezia, a result driven by two late own goals. This win allowed the champions to level with Lazio on 25 points. Meanwhile, Milan suffered their first league defeat of the season, falling 4-2 to Bologna at San Siro. Samuel Mbangula scored three goals in that match, while Alphadjo Cisse’s double for Milan was not enough to prevent the loss, ending their unbeaten streak.

The teams are set to meet in a highly anticipated Milan derby on Saturday. Inter will enter that fixture at the summit of the table, while Ruben Amorim’s side will look to bounce back from their recent home defeat.

title: Can Howe, Nagelsmann, or Pochettino End Manchester United's Doom Loop?
content:
The article questions whether elite coaches such as Mikel Arteta, Julian Nagelsmann, or Mauricio Pochettino can reverse Manchester United’s current decline. It argues that even top-tier managerial talent would face significant challenges at Old Trafford due to ongoing executive chaos and a squad described as unfit and uneven. The piece highlights the club’s rapid transition from a third-place finish to producing some of the worst football in its history, suggesting that the underlying instability was always present.

The author draws parallels to broader societal shifts, referencing the 2014 series of Celebrity Big Brother and the 2016 Brexit referendum to illustrate how perceived stability can be fragile. By comparing the public’s reaction to these events, the text implies that Manchester United’s recent struggles are not an isolated incident but rather a symptom of deeper, long-standing structural issues. The article posits that the club’s current difficulties are a result of foundations that were never solid, making it difficult for any new manager to effect immediate change without addressing these fundamental problems.
summary: The article argues that even elite coaches would struggle at Manchester United due to executive chaos and an unfit squad. It compares the club's recent decline from a third-place finish to historical examples of sudden societal shifts.

title: British Horseracing Authority warns budget tax hike may devastate sport
content:
Brant Dunshea, chief executive of the British Horseracing Authority, warned on Wednesday that a recent increase in the tax on fixed-odds gaming machines could have a “devastating” impact on horse racing. The British government, under Chancellor John Healey, raised the duty on profits from these machines in betting shops from 20% to 25% in his first budget. Dunshea stated that the sport’s ruling body will “urgently engage with the government to establish how we can work together to reduce the impact” of this change.

Although the 25% rate was significantly lower than the 40% doubling recommended by the Social Market Foundation thinktank earlier this year, Dunshea characterized the move as a “clear risk” to the industry. He cautioned that the tax hike could lead to the closure of “hundreds, if not thousands” of betting shops nationwide. This potential loss of venues poses a direct threat to the financial stability of the sport, prompting the call for immediate discussions with government officials to mitigate the consequences.
summary: Brant Dunshea, chief executive of the British Horseracing Authority, warned that raising the duty on fixed-odds gaming machines from 20% to 25% could lead to the closure of hundreds or thousands of betting shops. The sport's ruling body stated it will urgently engage with the government to reduce the impact of this budget decision.

title: Australia lead South Africa after Carey and Inglis counterpunch
content:
Australia secured a six-run lead against South Africa on the second day of their match in Cape Town, finishing the day at 330-4. The Australian innings was rebuilt by keepers Josh Inglis and Alex Carey, who pushed the team ahead of South Africa’s all-out total of 329. Despite two instances where South Africa produced double strikes to stall Australian progress, the visitors successfully rebuilt their position to hold onto six wickets for the start of day three.

The day’s play featured contrasting performances from the Australian openers. Travis Head played an aggressive first session, hitting seven boundaries with a mix of luck and skill, while his new partner Matthew Renshaw adopted a more defensive approach. Renshaw left and defended the new ball with clarity, a style that had previously characterized his middle-order play in Durban. The article notes that Renshaw was the original candidate to replace Jake Weatherald at the top of the order before the selectors' brief and ill-fated decision to select Nic Maddinson.
summary: Australia reached 330-4 at the close of the second day, overtaking South Africa's all-out total of 329. Keepers Josh Inglis and Alex Carey rebuilt the innings to put Australia in front with six wickets in hand.
