title: Reddit introduces new For You feed on homepage
content:
Reddit announced a change to its homepage feeds, introducing a new “feed experience” that will feature two distinct sections. The Following feed will display posts from the subreddits a user follows, while the For You feed will show posts from those same subreddits along with recommendations tied to a user’s interests.

Users who have already accessed the updated feeds report noticing the change, with one account owner seeing the new layout just yesterday. The shift is described as a significant adjustment for the platform, though it is not entirely unexpected given Reddit’s history of revising its homepage.

Earlier this year, Reddit also declared it would be deprecating the r/all feed, which previously surfaced posts from across the site. This move to a more personalized feed structure follows that announcement.
summary: Reddit is launching a new feed experience featuring a Following feed and a For You feed that shows posts from followed subreddits and recommendations related to users' interests. The change follows earlier announcements to deprecate r/all.
author: The Verge

title: Meta may delay new business terms again amid publisher backlash over AI training
content: Meta says it may push the implementation of its new business terms past November 20th as it faces backlash from publishers over concerns about AI training. In a post on X, Meta communications head Andy Stone said the company does "not plan to make policy changes without a full consultation with industry groups and leaders." The new business terms, which were supposed to take effect on October 30th, initially appeared to give Meta permission to train its AI models on the news sites that use Facebook and Instagram. Meta later changed its policies to remove language indicating that it could "train" its products on content scraped from these si …
summary: Meta may push the implementation of its new business terms past November 20th after publisher backlash over AI training. The terms, originally set to take effect on October 30, had been revised to remove language allowing Meta to train its AI on content scraped from news sites.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Launches First Touchscreen MacBook Pro at Pro and Tell Event
content: Apple’s “Pro and tell” event kicks off at 1PM ET / 10AM PT on October 28th. The event comes just a couple of weeks after Apple debuted the HomeView, its first smart display, and a little over a month after it announced the iPhone Duo, its first foldable. Its next event could feature yet another first for Apple: a MacBook with a touchscreen. A few devices received updates in the days leading up to the event. Apple announced an updated iPad Mini with a larger OLED display on Monday. The iMac and entry-level MacBook Pro were refreshed with M6 chips on Tuesday. Both are likely to pop up at Wednesday’s event, but their early announcement clears the way for a touchscreen MacBook to be the star of the show. This event will also continue a streak of product launches at Apple since John Ternus took over as its CEO on September 1st. So far, the flurry of new devices has also included the iPhone 18 Pro, new Apple Watches, the AirPods 5, and the HomePod Mini 2. Follow along here for all the latest news and updates. Touchscreen MacBook live blog: On the ground at Apple’s launch event Apple announces its first touchscreen MacBook Pro Apple refreshes the iMac with M6 chips Apple updates the MacBook Pro with M6 chips Apple’s Greg Joswiak teases an ‘exciting week.’ What to expect from Apple’s ‘Pro and tell’ event Apple teases MacBook Pro event next week
summary: Apple’s Pro and Tell event began at 1PM ET / 10AM PT on October 28th and unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro. The event also refreshed the iMac and entry‑level MacBook Pro with M6 chips and announced an updated iPad Mini with a larger OLED display.
author: The Verge

title: Apple to Debut Touchscreen MacBook Pro at Los Angeles Launch Event
content:
Apple’s week has been busy, with a new iPad Mini featuring an upgraded OLED display announced on Monday and M6 chip upgrades delivered for the MacBook Pro and iMac on Tuesday. The company’s Mac line has traditionally followed an iterative path, offering quiet refreshes that closely resemble their predecessors.

Today’s event in Los Angeles is expected to break that pattern. Apple is slated to unveil a revamped MacBook Pro that includes a touchscreen display—the first time a Mac will feature a true touchscreen, aside from the Touch Bar. The move would mark a significant shift for the brand, which has long criticized touchscreen laptops in its public statements.
summary: The MacBook Pro has looked mostly the same for several years now. And it’s never had a proper touchscreen.
author: The Verge

title: Chrome's enhanced autofill now draws Gmail data via Gemini to fill forms
content:
Chrome’s enhanced autofill has been upgraded to pull information from Gmail. Building on last year’s updates that added a user’s name, passport number, email address and physical addresses from Google Accounts and Google Wallet, the new feature now uses Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest data directly from Gmail.

Users can begin using the expanded autofill today. The feature can retrieve details such as shipment tracking numbers, flight booking numbers, hotel reservations, and other information found in confirmation emails, receipts or shipping updates, potentially eliminating the need to search those messages manually.
summary: Starting today, Chrome's enhanced autofill will use Gemini with Personal Intelligence to suggest information sourced from Gmail. The expanded feature can retrieve details such as shipment tracking numbers, flight booking numbers or hotel reservations, reducing the need to search for confirmation emails, receipts or shipping updates.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Unveils First Touchscreen MacBook Pro With OLED Display Starting At $2,899
content:
Apple unveiled its first touchscreen MacBook Pro at the “Pro and Tell” event on Wednesday. The 14‑inch model starts at $2,899 and will ship beginning November 16.

The new laptop features Apple’s “ProLED XDR” tandem OLED display, offering up to 2,000 nits of brightness, a 120 Hz refresh rate, and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. It is powered by M5 Pro or M5 Max chips—unlike the M6 chips on other MacBook Pros announced that week. CEO John Ternus noted the 14‑inch model weighs 3 pounds, and the glowing Apple logo on the lid has returned.
summary: Apple announced a new MacBook Pro featuring a tandem OLED touchscreen, M5 Pro or M5 Max chips, and a starting price of $2,899 for the 14-inch model. The laptop is available starting November 16th and includes a 120Hz display with up to 2,000 nits of brightness.
author: The Verge

title: Instagram has no plan to pay long-form video creators
content:
Instagram is testing long-form videos to attract creators from YouTube, but the platform has not established a plan to compensate them. Following Instagram head Adam Mosseri’s Monday announcement of the new Features, creators on Threads and Reddit expressed frustration over the absence of monetization options, contrasting this with YouTube’s ad share and performance-based incentives.

In a subsequent Threads post, Mosseri acknowledged the financial concerns, stating, "We understand the economics matter a ton, and are exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid." The specific details of these potential payment methods remain undetermined.
summary: Instagram is testing long-form videos to attract creators from YouTube but has not determined how or if it will pay them. Head Adam Mosseri stated the company is exploring multiple options to help long-form creators get paid.
author: The Verge

title: Apple Unveils OLED-Equipped 8th-Gen iPad Mini with New A20 Pro Chip
content:
Apple has announced the eighth‑generation iPad Mini, marking the first time the company’s smallest tablet will feature OLED technology. The new model sports an 8.5‑inch OLED display, the largest screen the Mini has ever had, while remaining thinner and lighter than the 2024 version. It is powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip, which the company says will deliver faster performance.

The iPad Mini will not hit retail shelves until November 6, but customers can already preorder it from Apple’s website. Preorders are available in several colors, with the starting price set at $699. The announcement was made alongside several new MacBook Pro models, underscoring Apple’s focus on expanding its high‑performance product line.
summary: Apple announced the eighth‑generation iPad Mini, the first Apple tablet to feature an OLED display. The device is available for preorder from Apple at $699, ships November 6, and runs the A20 Pro chip on an 8.5‑inch OLED screen that is larger than the 2024 model while being thinner and lighter.
author: The Verge

title: Antarctic sea ice decline drives rapid salinity shift in Southern Ocean
content:
Scientists report that the rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a significant shift in Earth’s climate system. In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp increase in salinity within Antarctic Intermediate Water, a vast layer of the Southern Ocean located between 2,300 and 4,000 feet deep. This change reverses decades of freshening and mirrors ocean shifts typically associated with major global climate changes over millennia, yet it is occurring within just a few years.

The implications of this salinity increase may extend beyond Antarctica. Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India, explained that this water layer spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans. As it moves, it transports heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics and across the equator.
summary: Researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in Antarctic Intermediate Water, reversing decades of freshening since 2016. This layer transports heat, carbon, and nutrients northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans.
author: Ars Technica

title: Nvidia launches free 40‑language transcription model
content: Nvidia has released a free speech-to-text model capable of transcribing up to 40 languages. The tool is designed for recordings rather than live audio, marking a significant advancement for meeting and medical transcription applications. Consequently, real-time transcription capabilities remain with competitors such as ElevenLabs.
summary: Nvidia released a free speech‑to‑text model that can transcribe up to 40 languages. The model works only on recordings, not live audio, leaving real‑time use to rivals such as ElevenLabs.
author: TechCrunch

title: DOE Grants $5B in Loans to Constellation Energy for Nuclear Reactor Modernization
content: Constellation Energy has secured $5 billion in government loans from the Department of Energy to modernize nuclear reactors. The majority of the new capacity generated by these upgrades is already committed to Google, Amazon, and Meta, which will utilize the power for their data centers.
summary: Constellation Energy will receive $5 billion in government loans to modernize its nuclear reactors. The new capacity is largely earmarked for Google, Amazon, and Meta.
author: TechCrunch

title: AI‑assisted coding fuels surge of bizarre video game mashups on social media
content: AI tools are making it easier to modify and recreate games, raising questions about piracy, copyright and how far the technology could disrupt the industry • Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here If your social media algorithms have clocked that you’re into video games, something strange will have happened in the past few weeks. Your feed, like mine, will have been full of clips of streamers playing bizarre mashups of popular video games. Skyrim in Minecraft. Halo, except the main character is Mario. Skate 2 in Call of Duty maps. A flood of professional-looking fan-coded game mods that are mildly interesting to look at for 30 seconds, but ultimately inconsequential. Would I download a mod that lets me play Wii Bowling inside a zombie shooter? No, but I am very interested in where they came from. Of course, the answer – or at least, most of the answer – is AI. After a week of researching this (thanks especially to Replay Mode on YouTube for this informative video, which set me down this track) I now understand that these mashup mods are not just AI-generated videos, but AI-assisted coding. Basically, as of a few weeks ago, Anthropic’s Claude has become extremely good at decompiling video game code. Games are written by humans in readable code and then compiled into binary 1s and 0s that the PC or console running it can read; decompiling is the reversal of that process, revealing a game’s source code, which humans can then edit and mess around with for fun. This used to be an extremely laborious process. But now it is not, because humans aren’t doing much of it any more.
summary: AI‑assisted coding fuels surge of bizarre video game mashups on social media.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Silicon Valley parents push to remove tech from their children's schools
content: Both private and public schools in tech regions are limiting the use of tech in classrooms. But will low-income districts be able to follow suit? German Gil spends most of his waking hours looking at screens. Since moving to the San Francisco Bay Area in 2015, the software engineer has bounced between startups and giants including Netflix, Facebook and GitHub. But when it came to the education of his daughter, Victoria, he wanted her to have a different experience, one in which his “kid could be a kid”.
summary: Both private and public schools in tech regions are limiting the use of tech in classrooms, raising questions about whether low‑income districts can follow suit. German Gil, a software engineer who has worked at Netflix, Facebook and GitHub, wants his daughter Victoria to have a different experience where she can be a kid.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ‘Light therapy without remortgaging the house’: the best LED face masks – tested
content:
LED face masks that use light therapy have surged in popularity, with many brands advertising that they can reduce fine lines, blemishes and redness. The devices are among the most expensive at‑home beauty products available, and some models combine different light wavelengths to boost their purported benefits.

In the article, the author consulted doctors and dermatologists and subjected several masks to testing. After this review, a new product was crowned the top choice.

The piece advises readers to remain cautious about costly, non‑invasive treatments and to conduct thorough research before purchasing. It stresses the importance of verifying claims through professional input rather than accepting marketing promises at face value.
summary: ‘Light therapy without remortgaging the house’: the best LED face masks – tested.
author: Guardian Technology

title: ‘Elonville’: US residents say Musk’s xAI offered to buy homes if they don’t sue over datacenter noise
content:
In Southaven, Mississippi, real estate agents have been canvassing homes on behalf of Elon Musk’s artificial‑intelligence venture, offering to purchase properties if owners agree not to join a lawsuit over noise from a nearby power plant. The agents reportedly targeted more than 400 residents in the neighborhood, many of whom have expressed discontent with the plant that powers the data center central to Musk’s AI ambitions.

Several homes close to the data center have already been bought by the company. A resident reported that the realtor outlined a plan to acquire additional houses in the area. The offer is tied to a condition that owners will not participate in legal action against the company regarding the plant’s noise.

Musk’s AI company officially became SpaceXAI in July and has recently been rebranded as SpaceXSI. However, neighbors of the Mississippi data center continue to refer to the firm as xAI.
summary: ‘Elonville’: US residents say Musk’s xAI offered to buy homes if they don’t sue over datacenter noise.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Azerbaijan hosts global experts at SOCGOV 2026 forum in Khankendi
content: Azerbaijan hosts global experts in Khankendi at the SOCGOV 2026 forum to debate digital and smart governance and explore technology solutions to improve public services.
summary: Global experts gathered in Khankendi for the SOCGOV 2026 forum. They debated the future of digital and smart governance and explored solutions to improve public services through technology.
author: Euronews

title: Texas Hispanic Trump supporters frustrated over economy, immigration before midterms
content: Hispanic voters in South Texas who supported Donald Trump in the 2024 election are voicing frustration with the economy, immigration policy and the cost of living as the United States approaches its midterm elections.
summary: Hispanic voters in South Texas who backed Donald Trump in 2024 are voicing frustration over the economy, immigration and the cost of living. Their comments come ahead of the US midterm elections.
author: Euronews

title: Trump rolls back methane rules for US oil and gas industry
content: Trump is rolling back methane regulations that affect the United States oil and gas industry. He says the move is intended to lower energy costs ahead of next week’s midterm elections, while rising oil prices—attributed to the U.S. war with Iran—are increasing voter frustration.
summary: Trump is rolling back methane rules for the US oil and gas industry. He is seeking to lower energy costs ahead of next week's midterm elections, as rising oil prices linked to the US war with Iran fuel voter frustration.
author: Euronews

title: Spain high-speed train crash near Toledo kills at least 68, rescue search continues
content:
Two high‑speed trains collided near Urda in Toledo province, central Spain, on Wednesday, 28 October. At least 68 people were killed and dozens more injured.

Rescuers are still searching the mangled wreckage, and authorities warn the death toll could rise further.
summary: At least 68 people were killed and dozens injured when two high‑speed trains collided near Urda in Toledo province on Wednesday, 28 October. Authorities said the death toll could rise as rescuers continued to search the wreckage.
author: Euronews

title: NYC Marathon set for Nov 1 with nearly 60,000 runners and millions of spectators
content: New York is set to become the running capital of the world this Sunday as the NYC Marathon kicks off on November 1. Nearly 60,000 participants are expected to line up at the start, and the event anticipates about two million spectators watching the race in the city. The marathon is described as one of the world’s most iconic races.
summary: New York will become the running capital of the world this Sunday. On November 1, nearly 60,000 people will line up at the start of the NYC Marathon, one of the world’s most iconic races.
author: Euronews

title: Lebanese expect little change in Israeli policy after election with no clear winner
content: Lebanese observers anticipate minimal shifts in Israeli policy following the recent elections, despite the ongoing Middle East conflict. As votes are tallied in Israel, no clear winner has yet emerged. The update is reported by France 24 correspondent Renée Davis.
summary: Lebanese expect little change in Israeli policy after Israel's elections. As votes are counted, no clear winner has emerged yet, France 24's correspondent Renée Davis reports the latest.
author: France 24

title: At least 64 killed as two Spanish high‑speed trains collide
content: At least 64 people died when two Spanish high‑speed trains collided on Wednesday. Rescue workers are still searching the wreckage for more bodies, marking Spain’s second fatal rail accident this year.
summary: At least 64 people died when two Spanish high‑speed trains collided on Wednesday. Rescue workers are scouring the wreckage for more bodies after Spain's second deadly rail accident this year.
author: France 24

title: Scotty Smart canvasses Atlanta to boost Black turnout for 2026 U.S. Midterms
content: The U.S. midterm elections will take place on November 3, 2026. In Atlanta, Georgia, activist Scotty Smart is traveling across the city to encourage Black voters to go to the polls. Facing widespread voter abstention, Smart aims to transform civic engagement into a powerful force for change.
summary: Scotty Smart canvasses Atlanta to boost Black turnout for 2026 U.S. Midterms.
author: France 24

title: John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell star in Martin McDonagh's 1973 Chile CIA thriller
content:
Four new films open in French cinemas this week, and arts24 critic Emma Jones has reviewed each of them. Among the releases is a political CIA thriller set in 1973 Chile that stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell.

Malkovich, a Volpi Cup for Best Actor winner at Venice, portrays a dying CIA agent in the Chilean drama. Jones called the film her favourite Martin McDonagh work since “In Bruges” and described it as a must‑see, while also noting McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” reunites the director with an A‑list cast.
summary: Martin McDonagh's film "Wild Horse Nine" features John Malkovich as a dying CIA agent in 1973 Chile alongside Sam Rockwell. Arts24 critic Emma Jones called it her favourite McDonagh film since "In Bruges" and a must‑see.
author: France 24

title: Israel election sees strong Arab party performance, potential kingmakers
content:
The election was uncertain, with no clear majority for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s right‑wing religious bloc or for his centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot’s coalition.

Arab parties delivered an unusually strong showing, positioning them as potential kingmakers in the Knesset.
summary: Israel’s election on Wednesday saw neither Netanyahu’s right‑wing religious bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot’s centrist bloc heading for a Knesset majority. An unusually strong performance by Arab parties could make them unexpected kingmakers.
author: France 24

title: Defeated candidate Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after fleeing Brazil
content:
Flavio Bolsonaro, the defeated Brazilian presidential candidate, landed in Miami on Wednesday, October 28, after fleeing Brazil with his family.  

He had spent 48 hours refusing to concede to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and threatened to attempt to annul the election result, according to France 24 correspondent Tim Vickery.
summary: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami on Wednesday, October 28, after fleeing Brazil. The move came after 48 hours in which Bolsonaro refused to concede to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and threatened to attempt to annul the election result.
author: France 24

title: Spain PM Sánchez addresses victims after Toledo train crash kills 64
content:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez addressed the nation from the site of the train collision in Toledo province, expressing full solidarity with the victims, their families, and the injured. The accident, which occurred on Wednesday, resulted in at least 64 deaths and 58 injuries. Rescue teams are currently searching the wreckage for survivors and bodies.

Earlier, Transport Minister Óscar Puente stated that a computer malfunction disrupted the railway’s safety system. He explained that the RENFE train was instructed to resume its journey despite an active stop signal before crashing into the stationary IRYO train. This incident marks Spain’s second deadly high-speed rail collision this year, following a January crash that killed 46 people.
summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez spoke at the Toledo province crash site, expressing solidarity with victims, families and the injured. Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer malfunction caused a RENFE train to ignore a stop signal and collide with a stationary IRYO train, killing at least 64 people and injuring 58.
author: France 24

title: Fighting in southern Ethiopia forces 50,000 to flee to Kenya
content: The United Nations reported Wednesday that an outbreak of fighting between rival forces in southern Ethiopia last week has forced some 50,000 people to seek refuge in neighbouring Kenya, citing local authorities.
summary: The outbreak of fighting between rival forces in southern Ethiopia last week led some 50,000 people to seek refuge in neighboring Kenya. The United Nations reported the displacement on Wednesday, citing local authorities.
author: France 24

title: Iran's future uncertain after Mecca alliance meeting, peace push from Saudi, Pakistan, Turkey
content: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have directed a new diplomatic initiative toward Tehran, presenting a peace push aimed at preventing further military escalation. While the outreach is officially framed as a de‑escalation effort, observers note it may also serve as a warning to Iran.
summary: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey have taken their latest peace push directly to Tehran. Officially it aims to avert a new military escalation, but the diplomatic outreach can also be seen as a warning to Iran.
author: DW World

title: Flavio Bolsonaro lands in Florida after fleeing Brazil amid money‑laundering probe
content: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida with his family early Wednesday. He left Brazil while facing money‑laundering allegations, doing so days after refusing to concede defeat to incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula.
summary: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Florida early on Wednesday. He fled Brazil days after refusing to concede defeat to incumbent Lula while facing money‑laundering allegations.
author: DW World

title: New Israeli government expected to bring little change for Arab neighbors, some positives
content: Experts say a new Israeli government is unlikely to produce major shifts on contentious issues such as Palestinian statehood and the presence of Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria. They add that while substantial change is not expected, a few modest positive developments could still emerge.
summary: Experts say a new Israeli government is unlikely to bring big changes on issues such as Palestinian statehood and Israeli troops in Lebanon and Syria. They add that a few small positive developments could still occur.
author: DW World

title: Tanzania families seek justice one year after post-election violence kills 518
content: One year after Tanzania’s deadly post‑election violence, families are still seeking answers. A government inquiry has recorded 518 deaths, and Deutsche Welle research has documented apparent use of excessive force by security forces.
summary: One year after Tanzania's deadly post-election violence, families are still seeking answers. A government inquiry recorded 518 deaths and DW research documented apparent use of excessive force by security forces.
author: DW World

title: UN warns ocean carbon uptake down 6% as climate change worsens
content: A new United Nations report warns that climate change has already cut the ocean’s capacity to absorb carbon by roughly six percent. The ocean continues to take up about 30 percent of human‑caused carbon dioxide emissions and around 90 percent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases, according to the report released ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November.
summary: The ocean absorbs around 30% of human‑caused carbon dioxide emissions and about 90% of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases. A new UN report warns that climate change has already reduced the ocean’s carbon‑absorption capacity by roughly six percent ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November.
author: UN News

title: UN-partnered report finds record 710,000 heat deaths in 2023, over 70% climate‑linked
content:
A UN‑partnered report released on Wednesday warns that climate inaction continues to harm and kill people worldwide, estimating a record 710,000 heat‑related deaths globally in 2023.  

For the first time, the report notes that more than seven in ten of those fatalities were attributable to human‑caused climate change.
summary: A UN-partnered report warned that an estimated 710,000 people died from heat worldwide in 2023, a record level. For the first time, more than seven in ten of those deaths were attributed to human‑caused climate change.
author: UN News

title: WHO calls for continued action as DRC Ebola cases exceed 10,000
content: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have risen above 10,000. The World Health Organization has called for sustained efforts to contain the disease’s spread.
summary: Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have surpassed 10,000. The World Health Organization said sustained efforts are needed to contain the disease.
author: UN News

title: Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi sentenced to 5 years, assets seized, travel ban imposed
content:
An Iranian court has imposed a new prison term on award‑winning film director Jafar Panahi, sentencing him to five years and one month in prison and ordering the seizure of all his assets. The 66‑year‑old, who received the Palme d’Or at Cannes last year for It Was Just an Accident, was sentenced in absentia, according to his lawyer Mostafa Nili.

In addition to the prison sentence, the court has placed a two‑year travel ban on Panahi and prohibited him from using social media for two years, Nili said in a statement to the Iranian news outlet Emtedad.
summary: An Iranian court sentenced award‑winning director Jafar Panahi to five years and one month in prison and ordered the seizure of all his assets. The court also imposed a two‑year travel ban and barred him from using social media for two years, according to his lawyer Mostafa Nili.
author: Guardian World

title: Serbian students bike to Strasbourg after Novi Sad protests over deadly railway roof collapse
content:
A movement that began in outrage has produced a notable election upset in Serbia, prompting observers to note that change is possible and to raise questions about what may follow.  

In April of last year, dozens of Serbian students embarked on a 13‑day bicycle trip from Novi Sad to Strasbourg, France, with the stated aim of making their voices heard in Europe and beyond. The students had been organizing near‑daily protests in Novi Sad after a deadly roof collapse at the city’s main railway station. Their demand for accountability and justice spread nationwide and was met with baton‑wielding police, tear‑gas and a political class that labeled the young demonstrators as traitors.
summary: In April of last year, dozens of Serbian students began a 13‑day bicycle ride to Strasbourg to amplify protests sparked by a deadly roof collapse at Novi Sad’s main railway station. Their nationwide push for accountability faced baton‑wielding police, teargas and accusations of treason, prompting an election upset and drawing European attention.
author: Guardian World

title: Andy Burnham says Tory Brexit deal is harsher than promised in 2016 referendum
content:
Prime Minister has cautioned cabinet members not to share opinions on the UK’s future relationship with Brussels before a formal review of options is undertaken.  

Andy Burnham, speaking to ministers at a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, warned that the current Brexit deal was “bad” and argued that the Conservative‑led agreement with the EU was more extreme than what was promised in the 2016 referendum. He subsequently wrote to frontbenchers outlining his hopes to move toward closer links with the EU.
summary: Andy Burnham warned ministers not to express opinions on how the government should approach Brexit, saying the Conservative deal with Brussels is more extreme than promised in the 2016 EU referendum. He told the cabinet the current deal is a bad one and wrote to frontbenchers outlining his hopes to address it.
author: Guardian World

title: 64 killed in second fatal high‑speed train crash in Spain within nine months
content:
Spain’s high‑speed rail network, described as the most extensive in Europe and the second largest worldwide after China, experienced its second fatal collision in nine months on Wednesday. Officials reported that at least 64 people were killed after two trains carrying a total of 544 passengers collided, causing several carriages to derail.

The crash has renewed safety concerns that were voiced before the earlier Toledo incident, a period during which train travel in the country has risen by 40%. The latest accident has placed Spain’s celebrated high‑speed system under renewed scrutiny.
summary: Officials said at least 64 people were killed on Wednesday morning after two trains collided on Spain’s high‑speed rail network. The collision involved two trains carrying 544 passengers and caused several carriages to derail, marking the second fatal crash in nine months.
author: Guardian World

title: Retired Admiral Peter Briggs says Australia must recruit hundreds for Aukus submarines
content: As USS Colorado showcases the program in Perth, Peter Briggs says personnel is just one of the ‘huge issues’ it faces Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast Australia faces an uphill battle to recruit and train enough naval personnel to serve on submarines planned for the future fleet of nuclear-powered vessels under the controversial $368bn Aukus deal, a retired admiral has warned. As the Virginia-class submarine USS Colorado arrived at HMAS Stirling south of Perth on Tuesday for a month of routine maintenance and to help build Australian expertise, retired admiral Peter Briggs said more people needed to be enrolled in the navy’s submarine program.
summary: Retired Admiral Peter Briggs says Australia must recruit hundreds for Aukus submarines.
author: Guardian World

title: Menindee Lakes hit five-year low, NSW imposes upstream water restrictions
content:
Water levels at the Menindee Lakes in western New South Wales have dropped to their lowest point in five years, with combined storage falling below 480 gigalitres earlier this month – the first time the figure has been that low since 2021. In response, the state government has imposed upstream water‑use restrictions.

Experts say the reduced volumes raise the risk of mass fish deaths over the summer, prompting the water‑restriction measures. The restrictions follow the recent decline in lake volumes below the 2021 level.
summary: Water levels at Menindee Lakes in western New South Wales have fallen to their lowest point in five years, with combined storage dropping below 480 gigalitres, the first time since 2021. The NSW government has imposed upstream water use restrictions and experts warn the low levels could cause mass fish deaths over summer.
author: Guardian World

title: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after Brazil election loss
content: A jet carrying Brazilian far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami, Florida, after the senator traveled from Brazil into Argentina and then flew via Ecuador. The aircraft, a Gulfstream IV registered LV‑JQW, departed Guayaquil, Ecuador, earlier in the day. Upon arrival, Bolsonaro, identified as the losing candidate in Sunday’s presidential election runoff, exited the airport under police escort and did not speak to the press.
summary: Far‑right senator Flávio Bolsonaro and his family landed in Miami, Florida, after crossing from Brazil into Argentina and then flying via Ecuador. The losing candidate in Sunday’s presidential election runoff left the airport under police escort without speaking to the press, and the Gulfstream IV jet, registered LV‑JQW, had departed Guayaquil earlier in the day.
author: Guardian World

title: Egypt fines Lina Attalah and orders shutdown of Mada Masr website
content:
Egyptian authorities fined Lina Attalah and ordered the shutdown of her independent news outlet Mada Masr. Attalah is identified as a prominent Egyptian journalist and the editor‑in‑chief of the outlet.

A Cairo court convicted her of managing an unlicensed website, leading to brief custody before her release by the authorities. The conviction and shutdown have prompted fresh international concerns over press freedom amid an intensifying crackdown on independent media in Egypt.
summary: Egyptian authorities fined journalist Lina Attalah and a court ordered the shutdown of her independent outlet Mada Masr after convicting her of managing an unlicensed website. Attalah was briefly detained by Cairo police before being released.
author: Guardian World

title: Israel election yields no clear winner despite highest turnout in nearly three decades
content: Israel’s recent election saw the highest voter turnout in almost thirty years, yet it produced no clear winner. The outcome leaves the country without a decisive result, prompting BBC journalist Yolande Knell to question its implications for Israel.
summary: Israel's elections produced no clear winner. The vote recorded the highest voter turnout in nearly three decades, prompting analysis by BBC's Yolande Knell.
author: BBC World

title: Deadly high‑speed train collision south of Madrid kills people, Spain's worst disaster since 2013
content: A Spanish high‑speed train collided with another train south of Madrid, killing people in what officials describe as the country’s worst disaster since 2013. The crash has prompted a scene of emergency response at the site.
summary: People have been killed after a Spanish high‑speed train collided with another train south of the capital Madrid. The crash is the country's worst disaster since 2013.
author: BBC World

title: Black holes can split in two only if spinning at maximum speed
content: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves. Now, new research suggests that the opposite may happen, too: single black holes may be able to split in two. But this can only happen if that progenitor black hole is spinning at maximum possible speed. That speed prevents the black holes from immediately falling back on each other. There are physical laws in place that would usually prevent black holes from splitting in two; the team behind this research investigated whether there are conditions in which these laws can be temporarily bypassed. One of the key aspects of physics that prevents black holes from bifurcating comes from thermodynamics. Black holes possess a characteristic called " entropy," which is essentially a measure of disorder within a system. Imagine a toddler's crayon box. When entropy is low, the crayons are neatly arranged by color. As entropy is increased, the crayons are scattered and no longer in order. To get the crayons back in order, it requires a parent to put energy into the system and neatly reorder the crayons. In other words, the entropy of a system can't be reduced without some intervention and energy being added from outside that system. Parenting would be a little easier if it could. A black hole splitting in two would represent a decrease in entropy, strongly disfavored by the laws of thermodynamics, but only if the black hole is not rotating. The situation could be different for a rapidly rotating black hole. This team of scientists found that a loophole exists for such a black hole. "The two resulting black holes must also be able to separate rather than immediately fall back together," team member Francesco Sannino of the University of Naples Federico II in Italy said in a statement. "When we include this requirement, the window largely closes again, except possibly for black holes rotating close to their maximum possible rate." Black hole trousers? The team calculated just how such a black hole split could occur, finding that the division of the black hole's outer boundary, or "event horizon," proceeds in an oddly trouser-like shape, with one resulting black hole slipping down each "leg." They termed this "pair-of-pants topologies." The researchers also determined that a split is more likely to take place if one of the resultant black holes is considerably smaller than its newly born twin. An illustration of a black hole splitting in two, creating the shape of pants. (Image credit: Francesco Sannino) "We cannot yet give a single probability for a black hole to split. It depends on how gravity behaves beyond Einstein's theory, and we are working to quantify this," Sannino said. "We expect small primordial black holes to be more prone to splitting than much larger astrophysical black holes." Sannino added that such black hole splits may be detectable in high-energy light called gamma-rays. "We may detect a split indirectly: gamma-ray telescopes such as Fermi-LAT can search for signals from tiny black-hole fragments that might form during mergers," the researcher concluded. The team's research was published on Oct. 22 in the journal Physical Review D.
summary: Scientists have long known that when two black holes collide, they merge to create a more massive black hole. These events are so violent that they set the very fabric of space ringing with ripples called gravitational waves.

title: La Bola Negra wins Cannes best director award, eyes Oscars
content: Oozing panache and bagging awards already, La Bola Negra is an eye-popping war and prejudice epic starring Penélope Cruz in a blond wig and Glenn Close speaking Spanish. We meet the ex-lovers who dreamed it up When Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo – the directing duo known in their native Spain as “Los Javis” – began writing their queer epic La Bola Negra, they weren’t thinking about whether it would be stylish (which it is) or win numerous awards (which it has) or capture what they refer to as “the anti-fascist zeitgeist” (which it does). Instead, they thought only of scale. “I’m done with LGBTQ+ movies being niche,” says Ambrossi. “I was like, ‘Let’s make the biggest, gayest war movie ever.’” Job done. At Cannes this year, the best director prize was awarded jointly to them and to Paweł Pawlikowski, who made the Thomas Mann road trip film Fatherland. La Bola Negra is now an Oscars frontrunner, with best picture and best director nominations all but guaranteed. Brimming with panache, the movie darts back and forth between three stories set in Spain: in 1932, a young man applying for membership of an exclusive casino is rejected on the grounds of his suspected homosexuality; in 1937, a callow nationalist soldier develops tender feelings for the injured republican prisoner under his watch; and in 2017, a queer historian inherits an unfinished story by Federico García Lorca. That story lends the movie its title and provides the thread that sews its strands together.
summary: La Bola Negra, a queer war epic directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, received the Cannes best director prize jointly with Paweł Pawlikowski. The film, starring Penélope Cruz and Glenn Close, is now an Oscars frontrunner with best picture and best director nominations all but guaranteed.

title: Ken Russell's 1971 film The Devils restored and rereleased after censorship
content:
Ken Russell’s 1971 film The Devils has been restored and rereleased in its complete form after years of censorship. The film, originally banned for obscenity, is described as a frenzied aria of confrontation and hysteria. It stars Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave, who are noted for delivering the performances of their lives in this scabrous classic.

Based on a true story of politically directed mass hysteria, the film was adapted by Russell from Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun and John Whiting’s stage play The Devils. The narrative centers on Father Urbain Grandier, a 17th-century French priest accused of witchcraft, a role played stylishly by Oliver Reed. In the film, Grandier declares, “I could never be Satan’s boy. I haven’t the humility.”

The review argues that while the film is obscene, the obscenity does not reside in the sexualized images of a crucified Christ or naked nuns. Instead, the text states that the violence of authority is what is shown to be obscene. Russell’s work is presented as a confrontational assault on good taste, depicting what punishments like burning at the stake might actually look like.

The film is situated in an era when movies in high-street cinemas retained the power to shock the polite cultural mainstream. This shock compelled serious discussion regarding whether the resulting ban or the film’s content was justified. The review highlights that the film underscores the violence of power through its intense depiction of these historical events.
summary: The film, based on a true story of mass hysteria and adapted from works by Aldous Huxley and John Whiting, features performances by Oliver Reed and Vanessa Redgrave. It was originally banned for obscenity but is now restored and rereleased in its complete form.

title: Jay-Z is the perfect Super Bowl shill for a league of billionaires
content: The rapper lends the NFL a veneer of credibility but is unlikely to push back on the establishment figures who run the league On Monday the NFL named Jay-Z as the headliner for this season’s Super Bowl half-time show. His company, Roc Nation, produces the show under a 2019 deal reportedly worth $5m a year, and the agreement was extended for another five years in 2024. NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said his one request when the partnership began was that Jay-Z “ take the stage himself one day “. Goodell’s wish makes total sense: Jay-Z is the perfect choice for the half-time show, and that’s not a compliment. The NFL wants a shill who can still pass for a rebel, and nobody in American music plays that part better than Jay-Z.
summary: Jay-Z is the perfect Super Bowl shill for a league of billionaires.

title: Norwegian federation president Lise Klaveness says Fifa can be reformed
content:
Lise Klaveness, the president of the Norwegian Football Federation, has stated that while she distances herself from the Fifa presidency, she believes the governing body is capable of reform. In an interview conducted in Oslo, Klaveness emphasized that the Norwegian federation possesses the right to speak and suggest changes, aiming to act as a “spearhead” in re-engaging with Fifa and other governing bodies.

The discussion centers on the topic of remedy, a human rights policy area that gained prominence following the World Cup in Qatar. Klaveness noted that the importance of this issue became clear when families of individuals injured or killed during the construction work leading up to the tournament were left without financial compensation. This outcome occurred after Fifa decided to direct a legacy fund to other purposes rather than providing direct compensation to these families.
summary: Lise Klaveness, president of the Norwegian Football Federation, states that people can challenge Fifa president Infantino. She wants to re-engage Fifa on the topic of remedy after families of injured or killed workers from the Qatar World Cup were left without financial compensation.

title: Rays defeat Brewers in 12th inning to avoid World Series sweep
content:
The Tampa Bay Rays avoided World Series elimination with a 4-3 victory over the Milwaukee Brewers on Tuesday night, forcing a decisive Game 5. The extra-innings rally came in the 12th inning, where Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour to make it 3-2. This was Pratt’s fourth hit of the game, occurring as Milwaukee neared a sweep and their first World Series title.

Jonny DeLuca and pinch-hitter Ben Williamson contributed RBIs during the stunning rally to secure the win. The result staved off elimination for Tampa Bay, though the Brewers still hold a 3-1 lead in the best-of-seven series.
summary: Tampa Bay Rays defeated the Milwaukee Brewers 4-3 in the 12th inning to force a Game 5 and stave off World Series elimination. Cooper Pratt hit a tiebreaking home run off Ian Seymour in the top of the 12th to give the Rays a 3-2 lead.

title: Jimmy Anderson to lead Napoli Knights in Rome T10 tournament
content:
Lancashire has announced it will not renew the contract of 44-year-old England cricketer Jimmy Anderson following a 25-year tenure. Despite this development, Anderson has not announced an immediate retirement. Instead, he expressed frustration through an Instagram post before remaining silent as he considered his future options.

The article describes Anderson as a player who refuses to bow out at the top, comparing his approach to that of tennis player Andy Murray. Both athletes are characterized by their desire to continue playing as long as their bodies allow. Anderson, identified as England’s leading Test wicket-taker, remains focused on dismissing opposition batsmen.

It is now confirmed that Anderson will lead and co-own the Napoli Knights for a 12-day T10 cricket tournament in Rome next month. This move follows his departure from Lancashire and represents one of the options he explored while considering his next steps in the sport.
summary: Jimmy Anderson will lead and co-own the Napoli Knights for a 12-day T10 cricket tournament in Rome next month. This move follows Lancashire's announcement that they will not renew his contract after 25 years.

The goalkeeper, Jay Lynch, was Fleetwood’s other hero, saving from Bruno Guimarães to set up the chance for victory. summary: Fleetwood Town defeated Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties in the Carabao Cup, with Conor Haughey scoring the winning kick. Arsenal's Max Dowman was sent off for retaliation, leaving the champions a man down during the shootout.

title: Economists Once Ignored Climate Crisis, Now Acknowledge Economic Threat
content:
The radical Stern report demonstrated that a low‑carbon future also makes economic sense. It argued that protecting the planet can benefit the economy, challenging the prevailing view that environmental costs are a burden.

Today, the article suggests that capitalism still needs a reminder that “saving the only planet we have makes good economic sense.” It notes that while there may be upfront costs, those expenses are justified to protect future generations from certain destruction. The piece stresses that a dead Earth offers no money to be made.

Two decades ago, mainstream economists held a different stance. They had argued that the climate crisis would be a mere economic blip, easily absorbed by growing economies and therefore not worth spending money on. In their accounting, ice caps and glaciers were considered functionally worthless, trees added to GDP only when cut down, and a livable climate did not merit a line on a spreadsheet. The article is written by Fiona Harvey, environment editor at the Guardian.
summary: Two decades ago, mainstream economists argued that the climate crisis would be a mere economic blip and not worth spending money on. The Stern report and other evidence now show that a low‑carbon future is economically beneficial and protecting the planet is essential for long‑term stability.

title: How blood vessels age from within
content:
Blood vessels form an extensive network that carries blood throughout the body, ensuring that oxygen, nutrients, and other essential substances reach even the most remote tissues. Each heartbeat propels blood through this system, delivering vital materials to cells in need.

The inner walls of these vessels are lined with a thin layer of specialized cells known as endothelial cells. These cells do more than provide a smooth surface; they regulate blood flow, control the passage of substances into surrounding tissues, and help coordinate responses to injury. Through these functions, endothelial cells play a crucial role in maintaining vascular health and overall bodily function.
summary: Blood vessels carry oxygen, nutrients, and other substances throughout the body. Their inner walls are lined with endothelial cells that regulate flow, control permeability, and coordinate injury responses.

content:
The first UK‑wide analysis of bowel screening for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has highlighted ways to improve early cancer detection. The study, described as the largest of its kind globally, examined how screening practices affect the discovery of potentially cancer‑forming growths.

Findings show that procedures carried out by professionals with regular experience, those that allow more time for the examination, and those that use a special dye to enhance visibility are each linked to a higher detection rate of small growths called polyps. These polyps can develop into cancer, underscoring the importance of these improved screening techniques.
summary: The first U. K.-wide analysis of bowel screening for patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) has identified opportunities to improve the early detection of cancer.

content: A new video on perimenopause notes that the topic has become widely discussed, with celebrities sharing personal experiences and doctors posting advice online. The program highlights that, alongside growing awareness, a rising number of women are encountering misinformation about treatments such as hormone‑replacement therapy (HRT). In the segment, Madeleine Finlay speaks with Dr Paula Briggs, a consultant in sexual and reproductive health, about why experts have raised an alarm. Science correspondent Nicola Davis then outlines the facts on perimenopause symptoms, testing and treatment options.
summary: Perimenopause is a hot topic with celebrities sharing experiences and doctors offering advice online. In the video, Madeleine Finlay talks to Dr Paula Briggs, a consultant in sexual and reproductive health, while Nicola Davis presents facts on symptoms, tests and treatments amid HRT misinformation.
author: Guardian Science

title: Scientists map 10,000-year sea‑level rise that turned inland hills into Venice lagoon
content:
Scientists have identified ancient hills and swamps that vanished as sea levels rose across the northern Adriatic. Their findings indicate that the ground beneath Venice, now famed as a floating city, once lay many miles inland.  

Research led by Samuele Ongaro of the University of Southampton and collaborators used seismic data and sedimentary cores from coastal basins in northern Italy, Slovenia and northern Croatia. The team modeled sea‑level changes and reconstructed the region’s landscape over the past 10,000 years, showing how rising waters reshaped the coastline and submerged former land.
summary: Scientists map 10,000-year sea‑level rise that turned inland hills into Venice lagoon.
author: Guardian Science

title: NASA Curiosity rover prepares to drill at Nazca site on Mars
content: Curiosity Navigation Curiosity Home Mission Overview Where is Curiosity? Mission Updates Science Overview Instruments Highlights Exploration Goals News and Features Multimedia Curiosity Raw Images Images Videos Audio Mosaics More Resources Mars Missions Mars Perseverance Rover Mars Curiosity Rover Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter Mars Odyssey More Mars Missions Mars Home 4 min read Curiosity Blog, Sols 5043-5049: Preparing to Drill at ‘Nazca’ NASA’s Mars rover Curiosity acquired this close-up image using its Mars Hand Lens Imager (MAHLI), showing the abundance of roughly disc-shaped potential crystal forms on our next drill target, informally named “Nazca.” The scratches made by the DRT brush are also visible in this image. MAHLI, located on the turret at the end of the rover’s robotic arm, uses an onboard focusing process to make a composite of images of the same target acquired at different focus positions, to bring multiple features into focus in a single image. Curiosity composed the image on Oct. 18, 2026, Sol 5048 (Martian day 5,048 of the Mars Science Laboratory Mission), at 12:19:51 UTC. NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS Written by Lucy Lim, Planetary Scientist at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center Earth planning date: Friday, Oct. 16, 2026 Following the Basque Lakes drill campaign, Curiosity has returned to a spot just a few meters away from the “Chiu Chiu” block to conduct our next drill campaign. “Chiu Chiu” itself wasn’t a good candidate for drilling but the block just beyond it was much more promising, so it became our drive target during Monday’s planning. I was on planning Friday as Geology and Mineralogy Science Theme Lead when we received our close-up views of the neighbor block from the post-drive imaging and our team was happy to see that it was jam-packed with the “disc- and needle-” shaped lumps, just like “Chiu Chiu.” We quickly gave the science go-ahead to proceed with preparations for drilling at the newly named “Nazca” site. One major hypothesis about how the “discs and needles” texture formed is that the characteristic shapes were originally created during the growth of crystals, or “crystal forms.” Minerals will tend to grow into specific shapes depending on their microscopic crystal structure, similar to the salt crystals that you can grow in your kitchen as a home science project. (Maybe you have grown one of those for a science class in school!) The relatively large sizes of the crystal forms at “Nazca” and “Chiu Chiu” are providing clues about the temperature at the time when they grew and the availability of salts and fluids. However, we can’t necessarily assume that the modern-day composition represents the original mineral because sometimes mineral crystals are replaced by other minerals some time after original crystallization. The new minerals are then known as “pseudomorphs” because they have the same shape as the first minerals but not the same composition or molecular structure. As we prepared for the drill preload test, we also planned several special observations aimed at highly detailed characterization of the crystal forms. MAHLI will execute a Quantitative Relief Model (“QRM”) observation consisting of five overlapping images at slightly different geometries. The combination of these will enable a detailed three-dimensional relief model to be constructed. In addition, MAHLI will also add extra frames to its highest-resolution imaging by doubling the number of focus mechanism steps. Together, these observations will increase the resolution of the 3D models we will have of the crystal forms. Meanwhile, the ChemCam LIBS will conduct a “depth profile” experiment to obtain compositional information from slightly deeper layers within a nearby crystal-form-rich target, “Toucan”. Normally the 150 LIBS laser shots from each sol’s observation are spaced out over a five-point raster at 30 shots per point, but this time we are concentrating all 150 laser shots on the same spot on the rock. Since each laser shot vaporizes a very small amount of the rock to form a plasma, the 150-shot profile should penetrate approximately five times deeper than a normal 30-shot point observation. We will thus be able to observe the composition deeper inside the exposed crystal form and see whether it’s different from the surface-level composition. There are several reasons this could be the case including exposure of the surface to the modern Martian environment and also the circumstances in which the crystal form developed originally, so it’s an experiment worth pursuing. The LIBS, DRT and APXS will also be applied to the “Nazca” spot before the preload test to characterize its surface composition as thoroughly as possible before drilling. The third LIBS of the plan will go to “Condor,” a nearby block in which a finely layered texture is exposed. We also continued to observe the modern Martian environment as twilight cloud season begins. In this plan we included some nighttime imaging of the larger and brighter of Mars’ two satellites, Phobos. Capturing images of Phobos and the nearby sky when Phobos is full can show sunlight reflecting off the moon and scattering in the Martian atmosphere, providing a good way to estimate the particle sizes in the Martian clouds. We can do similar measurements sometimes with solar observations, but the Phobos data allow us to measure cloud particle sizes later in the night. We expect to be measuring high-altitude carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) clouds in this observation. Want to read more posts from the Curiosity team? title: ICE's HSI runs one of the largest anti‑left surveillance operations in US
content: ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is conducting extensive surveillance of left‑wing activists, a program described as rivaling the FBI and CIA’s historic crackdowns on the civil‑rights and anti‑war movements. The operation is characterized as one of the largest anti‑left surveillance efforts in U.S. history.
summary: ICE’s Homeland Security Investigations is conducting far‑reaching spying against left‑wing activists. The operation is described as rivaling FBI and CIA crackdowns on the Civil Rights and anti‑war movements.
author: Wired

title: Men spend $50,000 to reserve a Tesla Roadster as base model costs far more
content: The base model—without thrusters or the flight system—will likely cost several times that amount to buy. “I’m going to do everything in my power to get the flying one,” says one customer.
summary: Some men are paying $50,000 to reserve a Tesla Roadster. The base model without thrusters or a flight system would likely cost several times that amount, and one customer said he will do everything to get the flying version.
author: Wired

title: Portland Fermentation Festival held last week as sauerkraut, kimchi gain spotlight
content: The annual Portland Fermentation Festival took place last week in Oregon, at a time when sauerkraut, kimchi, and other funky foods are in the social and political spotlight.
summary: The annual Portland Fermentation Festival was held last week in Oregon. Sauerkraut, kimchi and other fermented foods are currently in the social and political spotlight.
author: Wired

title: Meta launches “Waddle World” AI pet journal app
content:
Meta has quietly launched a new app called Waddle World. The app is described as a “tamagotchi‑style” pet game in which virtual creatures chat with users and create doodles to illustrate those conversations.

According to its Apple and Play Store listings, the 16‑bit pet care game is actually “a daily journal disguised as a pet.” Users are encouraged to talk, not type, to their pixel pets, and can also play “cozy games” such as stacking groceries or word games. The Play Store description calls the experience “a little friend that listens” and a cozy world where a hatchable virtual pet lives, inviting users to visit whenever they like.
summary: Meta has launched a tamagotchi‑style pet game called Waddle World that is described as a daily journal disguised as a pet. The virtual pets chat with users, create doodles and offer cozy activities such as stacking groceries or word games.
author: The Verge

title: Meta considered whisper strategy to turn academics against Jonathan Haidt
content:
Meta was feeling public pressure over teen mental health and facing an impending onslaught of kids safety trials, the company considered a campaign to discredit a key critic: social psychologist Jonathan Haidt.  

Newly filed court documents show that in March 2023, Meta discussed a “Whisper strategy” to “turn academics against Haidt,” a thought leader who blamed social media for rising adolescent depression and anxiety.  

Haidt hadn’t yet published his bestselling book, The Anxious Generation, but he testified about his conclusions before Congress in 2022, and in February 2023, he began posting more of his theories and research to Substack.
summary: Meta considered a "whisper strategy" to turn academics against social psychologist Jonathan Haidt in March 2023, according to newly filed court documents. Haidt had testified before Congress in 2022 about social media's role in adolescent depression and anxiety, and began publishing his theories on Substack in February 2023.
author: The Verge

title: South Africa tests 7.6-kilometre freight train in bid to break world record
content: South Africa’s state‑owned logistics firm Transnet reported that it tested a freight train measuring 7.6 kilometres in length, composed of 696 empty wagons. The train was run over an 860‑kilometre route from Saldanha Bay to an inland iron‑ore mine, a trial Transnet described as the world’s longest freight train.
summary: Transnet tested the world's longest freight train, measuring 7.6 kilometres and consisting of 696 empty wagons. The train travelled 860 kilometres from Saldanha Bay to an inland iron ore mine.
author: Euronews

title: Israel election deadlock; Finland and Norway leaders call Putin
content:
Israel’s recent election has ended in a clear deadlock, with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot positioned to secure a majority.  

In Europe, Finland’s and Norway’s leaders have called Vladimir Putin as the continent seeks a seat at the table. The coverage also notes Serbia’s vote, the upcoming U.S. mid‑terms, and Mbappé’s dispute with China.
summary: Israel's election ended in apparent deadlock with neither Benjamin Netanyahu nor Gadi Eisenkot on track for a majority. Leaders of Finland and Norway have phoned Vladimir Putin as Europe seeks a seat at the table.
author: Euronews

title: Russian drone strike in Kharkiv injures five, sparks building fires
content:
A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv injured five people, including a 4‑year‑old child.  

The attack set several buildings ablaze, and firefighters were working under the threat of further strikes.
summary: A Russian drone strike on Kharkiv overnight injured five people, including a 4-year-old child. The attack set several buildings on fire, and firefighters are battling the blazes amid the threat of additional strikes.
author: Euronews

title: Brazil's President Lula celebrates 81st birthday after re‑election win
content: Brazil’s re‑elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva marked his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October, surrounded by dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília. The celebration came just two days after he won a closely contested election.
summary: Brazil's re‑elected President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his 81st birthday on Tuesday, 27 October. He was joined by dozens of supporters outside the Alvorada presidential palace in Brasília, two days after his closely contested election victory.
author: Euronews
